items.title: Close the gap beside the portico where the sea shows through
items.for_owner: On each side of the clock tower's entrance porch, a thin strip of sea and sky shows between the porch and the three-storey blocks. It becomes a set-back, shaded wall joining them, as on the real campus. This goes with #2.
items.code: campus(), before line 184 (the first isl-vwall): const link = rect(cx - 6.9*u, iTop + 0.5*u, 13.8*u, base - iTop - 0.5*u); s += `<path class="isl-vshade" d="${link}"/>`; It is drawn first, so the walls, portico and roofs cover everything except the two gaps; one winding. Leave out the optional windows. Depends on #2's --isl-vshade values.

items.title: Campus shade is lighter than its walls at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk
items.for_owner: The shaded end walls of the outer wings are paler than the lit fronts at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk, and at Night they barely differ, so they look lit from the wrong side. The shade tone moves a step darker than the walls. Day does not change, and #1 needs this.
items.code: layout-art.css line 762: --isl-vshade #707d8e -> #55524d; line 766: #253449 -> #20242b. Only campus() (island-vignettes.js line 185) uses isl-vshade, and only the hero uses campus(). Check Dawn, Sunset and Dusk afterwards.

items.title: String course crosses the shaded side face lit
items.for_owner: On the Governance picture, the stone band between the two floors still crosses the building's shaded side as a light stripe, while the cornice and parapet above it now turn into shade. Its side portion gets shaded too, so the corner you liked turns all the way down.
items.code: courtHouse(), after line 1192 (it must follow the band at 1191, which covers the earlier turn shade): s += `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="${turn(mid - Y(0.004), mid + Y(0.016), Y(0.006))}"/>`;

items.title: The Sunset clock shows two hour hands
items.for_owner: At Sunset the This Week clock shows two hour hands, one at 6:30 and one at 7:30. The 7:30 hand will show only at Dusk, as intended.

'' : cls} isl-chand" .../>`; s += cls === 'isl-d' ? `<g class="isl-lq" data-q="d">${p}</g>` : p; (uses .isl-lq rules at layout-art.css 528-532). CSS alternative: .isl[data-sky="sunset"] .isl-chand.isl-d { display: none; }. No rng.

items.title: Masthead and bow lights do not follow the heeled rig
items.for_owner: On News & Events, each yacht's white masthead light hangs in the sky beside its mast top, and the red and green bow lights float above the bows, because the lights were not tilted with the leaning boats. They move onto the mast top and the bow. The green light goes, because a boat seen side-on sailing left shows only its red (port) side.
items.code: regatta(), yacht(), line 713: const a = heel*Math.PI/180, ca = Math.cos(a), sa = Math.sin(a), rot = (px, py) => [x + (px - x)*ca - (py - wl)*sa, wl + (px - x)*sa + (py - wl)*ca]; lights[0].push([...rot(x - L*0.5, wl - hh), 'r'], [...rot(mx, wl - hh - mh*1.02), 'w']); omit the 'g' push. The halos at line 726 follow automatically. Tell the owner the green is removed on purpose.

items.title: Boiling-house arches break through the broken wall top
items.for_owner: On Tools & Prompts, the ruined boiling house's arches poke up through its broken wall top as little domes, so at 1440 it looks like a row of small huts. The wall top rises a little so each arch has stone over it. The gable keeps its height, and the stone joint lines stop at the openings instead of crossing the fields seen through them.
items.code: bettysHope(): line 1048 top `bTop - Y(0.03) + r()*Y(0.03)` (still one r() per point); lines 1051-1052 ar = bwid*0.065 and spring bBase - Y(0.04) in both V commands; lift the gable peak Y(0.575)->Y(0.545) and shoulder Y(0.615)->Y(0.585). Course loop (line 1056): build each line as segments that skip cx±ar below the spring and cx±sqrt(ar^2 - (spring - y)^2) in the arch head. Render 1440 Day before and after.

items.title: The sea shows between the town houses down to the street
items.for_owner: On Governance, thin strips of harbour, ripples included, show between the town houses right down to the pavement, which puts the Court House on the waterfront. A shaded back row of walls goes in behind the houses, so the gaps read as alleys and only sky shows above the roofs.
items.code: courtHouse(), before the town walls (line 1163): const back = `M${F(X(-0.03))} ${F(street)}V${F(v.y0 - Y(0.012))}H${F(X(1.03))}V${F(street)}Z`; s += `<path class="isl-tw0" d="${back}"/><path class="isl-vpshade" d="${back}"/>`; No r() call, so the town is unchanged. It also covers the sea triangles beside low roofs and follows the horizon. Check the Sunset disc stays above the roofs.

items.title: Far houses and lights sit between and on the cathedral's towers
items.for_owner: On About, by Day a tiny far house sits between the cathedral's twin towers, and at night far lights are painted on the towers' stone. Far houses and lights stay out of the cathedral's column, so the towers stand clean against the hill.

One filter covers the Day houses and the night lights.

items.title: The middle boat hides behind the window's mullion
items.for_owner: On Tool Directory, the middle boat in the window sits right behind the centre window bar. Its mast and light are hidden, while its hull and a column of light on the water still show. It moves left into open water.
items.code: toolWall line 1854: [0.5, 0.06, 0.7] -> [0.4, 0.06, 0.7]. The r() count is unchanged, so nothing else moves.

items.title: The transom cuts the rising Sun in half at Dawn
items.for_owner: On Learning to Prompt, the window's crossbar runs straight through the middle of the rising Sun at Dawn. The crossbar rises to make a small top light, so the Sun sits whole below it, and the Moon's place moves to the centre of the smaller top pane.
items.code: promptDesk line 1993: (wB - wT)*0.42 -> (wB - wT)*0.30. PIECES['prompt-desk'].moonAt (line 3010): y -> (f.wT + (f.hz - f.wT)*0.22)/H. Re-render Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120. If a narrow width is tight, use the adaptive form: transom y = min(0.42 frac, hz - SKY.a.sun[1]*ppd - 1.12*sunR(W) - 4), with the Moon centred in the resulting upper pane.

items.title: The far shore's lights are missing; only their columns are drawn
items.for_owner: On Step-by-Step Guides, at dusk and night twelve columns of light run down the water from the far shore, but the shore has no lights on it. The lights get drawn and placed on the land, which also puts the daytime houses at those spots on the land.
items.code: steps(), lines 757-763: add topAt(x) interpolating farShore[0..5] (already in px). In the loop, keep the same two r() calls: const x = X(0.01 + r()*0.3), t = topAt(x); shoreLights.push([x, t + (Y(0.6) - t)*(0.25 + r()*0.5)]). After 763: s += `<path class="s-vlight isl-vwin" style="--i:0" d="${lightsD(shoreLights)}" stroke-width="1.3"/>`; (s-vlight is hidden by Day).

items.title: Quoins stick out of the tower as see-through blocks and are out of step

They also drift out of step with the stone courses. Each corner stone becomes one course tall and flush with the corner, and a low plinth at the foot stands the tower on the square.

items.title: Day blurs cut into boxes; flank shade spills off the land
items.for_owner: On For Students by Day, several soft blurs are cut into boxes: a straight-edged patch of shallows left of Galleon Beach, a flat-topped grey haze above the range, and hill shade spilling onto the water and sky. Two thin shade wedges on small bumps also read as light shafts. The blurs will fade freely, the shade will stay on the hills, and only the main peak gets shaded.

Line 426: <clipPath id="islvrangec"><path d="${poly(range)}"/></clipPath><g class="isl-ydet" clip-path="url(#islvrangec)">${flanks(range.slice(0, 10), Yp(0.28))}</g> (main peak only; leave makeKit.flanks alone, since a 0.03H threshold would also drop the headland's flank). Re-render Day at 1920 and 1440, and check the shallows do not creep up the town shore.

items.title: The caption names Montserrat, but the island drawn is Nevis
items.for_owner: On For Faculty & Staff, the caption says Montserrat is on the horizon, but the single cone drawn is Nevis at its true bearing; Montserrat lies well outside this view. Proposed caption, for your yes: "The view from Curtain Bluff, with Nevis on the horizon".
items.code: data/art_slots.yaml line 102: caption: "The view from Curtain Bluff, with Nevis on the horizon". Correct the note at lines 47-51: Montserrat is visible from the bluff but about 20 degrees left of this frame; the left edge is at about 261 degrees and Nevis at 0.18W (island-core.js SKY.d.sun, NEVIS_L = 280, PIECES['curtain-bluff'].ppd). The file is owner-owned, so quote the label and wait for his yes. No drawing change.

items.title: The red pent roof across each inner block
items.for_owner: On the homepage, add the narrow red roof that runs across each three-storey block between its top two floors. It is one of the campus's signature features in every front photo, and it replaces the thin grey rail there now.

Line 143: keep only the iTop + 7.6u rail. The window-row clearances are 2 to 3.5 px, so check at 1440.

items.title: Drive lamps: heads by Day
items.for_owner: On the homepage by Day, the four drive lamp posts are bare dark sticks with nothing on top, so they read as downpipes. Each gets a small cap and an unlit lamp head by Day, and the evening lights stay exactly as they are.

Optional: pool(lx, ly + 0.3*u, 2.6*u, 0.6*u, 0.6) in glows; check it does not wash over the arcade's foot.

The r() sequence changes for the skipped windows, so re-check which ones are lit.

items.title: The mug keeps its evening white at Night
items.for_owner: At Night, on This Week and on Learning to Prompt, the mug keeps its evening white and outshines the paper beside it, so it looks switched on. It gets a Night tone, darkened the same way the paper is.
items.code: layout-art.css after line 540: [data-md-color-scheme="slate"] .isl:where(:not([data-sky])), .isl[data-sky="night"] { --isl-lmug: #a7a399; } The .isl-lmug and .isl-lmugh rules (548-549) pick it up. The library's mugs are hidden at Night, so only these two pieces change.

items.title: The lampshade's underside is missing by Day
items.for_owner: On Committee Work by Day, the lampshade has a flat bottom, as if seen at eye level, while the table below is seen from above. The shade's dark open underside will always show; from Dawn to Night the glowing underside covers it as now.
items.code: committeeRoom(), after the lbronze rim (2672) and before the tbulb group (2673): + `<path class="isl-cshade" d="${polyD(under)}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${polyD(under)}"/>`.

items.title: Hang the drip bag from its hook, with a drip chamber
items.for_owner: On Clinical Practice, the drip bag floats a few pixels below the stand's hook bar with nothing joining them. A short hanger goes in, plus the small drip chamber under the bag that makes it read as an IV set.
items.code: hospitalRoom(), lines 2332-2336: after the pole `<path class="isl-hframe" d="M${F(ix + Y(0.05))} ${F(iT + Y(0.01))}V${F(bagT + Y(0.004))}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(0.8, Y(0.007)))}"/>`; after the fluid `<path class="isl-hbag" d="${rect(ix + Y(0.043), bagB - Y(0.006), Y(0.014), Y(0.036))}"/>`; in the isl-hcord line change the start ${F(bagB)} -> ${F(bagB + Y(0.03))}.

items.title: The sailing boat's light has no column and the boat no reflection
items.for_owner: On Learning to Prompt, the sailboat's masthead light comes on at dusk with nothing on the water beneath it, and the bright sail has no reflection, while the island beside it has both. It gets its column of light and a faint reflection.
items.code: promptDesk after line 1985: const hull = (the existing hull string), sail = (the existing sail string); s += dashes(streakList(sb, sy + 1, H, rng(617), 0.04, 0.05), 's-vglow', 1, [0.08, 0.16, 0.3]) + `<g opacity=".15"><g transform="translate(0 ${F(2*sy)}) scale(1 -1)"><path class="isl-vhull" d="${hull}"/><path class="isl-vsail" d="${sail}"/></g></g>`; Use its own rng, since r feeds the handwriting, book offsets and sparks.

items.title: The transom bar crosses the top of the setting Sun
items.for_owner: On Tool Directory at Sunset, the window's crossbar cuts across the top of the setting Sun. The Sun is set three minutes later and a little further right in the window, so it sits whole under the bar and still stands on the hill.
items.code: PIECES['tool-wall'] (line 2993): sunset '18:23' -> '18:26' AND face (line 2995) f.ww*0.7 -> f.ww*0.86 (the time change alone sinks about 30% of the disc into the hill). Update the PIECES comment. Re-render Sunset and Dusk at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120; if 2.4 px of clearance at 1920 reads as touching, use 18:27.

items.title: Wall joints in uneven pairs, one row only, one spilling onto the guardhouse
items.for_owner: On Courses and Resources, the stone wall's vertical joints come in uneven pairs on one row only, and at 1440 one stray joint lands on the guardhouse. Two properly staggered rows go in, with every joint kept inside the wall.
items.code: telescope(), lines 990-992: for (let row = 0; row < 2; row++) for (let x = wx0 + Y(0.05) - row*Y(0.025); x < wx1 - 1; x += Y(0.05)) if (x > wx0 + 1) wj += `M${F(x)} ${F(wTop + Y(row ? 0.045 : 0.018))}v${F(Y(row ? 0.035 : 0.027))}`; (row 2 kept short so it stays above the foot).

items.title: The station's left end hangs over the falling slope
items.for_owner: On General AI, a small wedge of sky shows under the left end of the ground station, where the hill falls away. A concrete footing carries the building down to the slope there.
items.code: dishNet: hoist const bx = X(0.64), bT = Y(0.58), bw = Y(0.36) from line 2431 to above line 2427 (to avoid a TDZ error); before the land path: s += `<path class="isl-aramp" d="${rect(bx, bT + Y(0.14) - 1, bw, Y(0.08))}"/>`; The land hides all of it except the wedge above the slope. Use isl-tw0 instead of isl-aramp if #47 is not taken.

items.title: A concrete base course so the station stands off the hill after dark
items.for_owner: On General AI, in every version except Day, the ground station is exactly the hill's colour and melts into it, so it reads as a knoll with windows. A low concrete base course along its foot will show its ground line in every version.
items.code: dishNet, as its own statement right after the station's walls, roof and windows (lines 2432-2433): s += `<path class="isl-aramp" d="${rect(bx - Y(0.004), bT + Y(0.126), bw + Y(0.008), Y(0.014))}"/>`; The windows end at bT + 0.10H, so nothing is covered. If #106 lands, end its door at bT + Y(0.126).

items.title: Let the planter read: pour it in the ramp's concrete with a lit lip
items.for_owner: On Accessibility, the planter by the steps is the same colour as the wall behind it in every version, so the shrubs and palm seem to sit on a ledge of the wall. It becomes the same poured concrete as the ramp and steps, with a lit top edge and a shadow at its foot.
items.code: wayIn line 2816: class="isl-vstone" -> class="isl-aramp" on rect(pl0, street - Y(0.06), W, Y(0.06)); then, before the shrubs() call: `<path class="isl-vstep-edge" d="M${F(pl0)} ${F(street - Y(0.06))}H${F(W + 2)}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1.6, Y(0.01)))}"/><path class="isl-vpshade" d="${rect(pl0, street - Y(0.008), W, Y(0.01))}"/>`.

items.title: The tower's roof: a low hipped roof with white cresting, not a tall pyramid
items.for_owner: On the homepage, the clock tower has a tall pointed roof, but every campus photo shows a low red hipped roof with a flat ridge and a white cresting. The roof gets redrawn low, with the cresting, and shown to you side by side with the present one, because it changes the picture's focal outline.
items.code: campus(), line 158: const e = shaftTop - lookH - 0.8*u; roofs += `M${F(tx0 - 1.4*u)} ${F(e)}L${F(tx0 + 1.8*u)} ${F(e - 2.1*u)}H${F(tx0 + tw - 1.8*u)}L${F(tx0 + tw + 1.4*u)} ${F(e)}Z`; after line 159: posts += rect(tx0 + 1.8*u, e - 2.55*u, tw - 3.6*u, 0.5*u); (cream, drawn after the roofs). The top falls to about base - 37.9u, inside heroScene's box (base - 42u). Present as a before and after.

items.title: The skeleton's shadow on the wall
items.for_owner: On Medical Education by Day, the skeleton almost vanishes into the pale wall, so only its eye holes and stand read, and its legs fade at Sunset and Dawn. A faint shadow on the wall, offset only slightly, gives each bone a thin shaded edge.
items.code: lectureHall(): factor the skull and pelvis fill path (2403-2404) into const bonesF; before line 2401: s += `<g transform="translate(${F(Y(0.005))} ${F(Y(0.007))})"><path class="isl-mbshadow" d="${bones}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1, u*0.2))}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${bonesF}"/></g>`; layout-art.css near line 664: .isl .isl-mbshadow { stroke: var(--isl-lside); stroke-opacity: 0.22; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } Give the stand no shadow. Check the rib cage at 1920 Day and 1440 Sunset.

items.title: The white-trimmed gablet in the portico roof
items.for_owner: On the homepage, add the small white-trimmed gable at the centre of the entrance porch's red roof. It is the porch's one distinguishing mark in every campus photo.
items.code: campus(), after line 187: s += `<path class="isl-vwall" d="${polyD([[cx - 1.7*u, pTop - 0.15*u], [cx, pTop - 1.35*u], [cx + 1.7*u, pTop - 0.15*u]])}"/><path class="isl-vroof2" d="${polyD([[cx - 1.15*u, pTop - 0.35*u], [cx, pTop - 1.05*u], [cx + 1.15*u, pTop - 0.35*u]])}"/>`; (raised 0.3u from the original proposal to match the photos, still inside the roof triangle, whose apex is at pTop - 2.6u). At Night it nearly vanishes, which is acceptable.

items.title: The reading lamp's lit underside
items.for_owner: On Clinical Practice, the reading lamp over the bed casts a halo and a cone of light but shows no light source, and by Day it is a brown box on the wall. The shade gets an open underside that glows from Dawn to Night and is dark by Day, like the committee room's lamp.
items.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2350, after the isl-cshade path: + `<ellipse class="isl-cshade" cx="${F(lx)}" cy="${F(ly + Y(0.04))}" rx="${F(Y(0.058))}" ry="${F(Y(0.01))}"/><ellipse class="isl-tdrop" cx="${F(lx)}" cy="${F(ly + Y(0.04))}" rx="${F(Y(0.058))}" ry="${F(Y(0.01))}"/>` + `<g class="isl-vlamps isl-vwin" style="--i:1"><ellipse class="isl-tbulb" cx="${F(lx)}" cy="${F(ly + Y(0.04))}" rx="${F(Y(0.058))}" ry="${F(Y(0.01))}"/></g>`. Precedent: committee room lines 2669 and 2673.

items.title: The sconce's own light: the lit mouth under its shade
items.for_owner: On This Week, the wall lamp throws a halo and a cone of light, but its shade shows no glowing opening, and the cone spills a haze across the window glass. The lit opening goes in under the shade, and the cone stays on the wall between the calendar and the window.
items.code: weekCalendar line 2291, inside <g class="isl-vlamps isl-vwin" style="--i:1"> before the shade (2292): + `<ellipse class="isl-tbulb" cx="${F(lx)}" cy="${F(ly + Y(0.07))}" rx="${F(Y(0.026))}" ry="${F(Y(0.008))}"/>`. Cone foot: const cf = Math.min(Y(0.12), (f.wx0 - (cx0 + cw))/2 - Y(0.012)); use [lx + cf, Y(0.62)] and [lx - cf, Y(0.62)]. Check Night and Dusk at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120.

items.title: Quoins returning round the corner onto the side face
items.for_owner: On Governance, the corner stones at the building's right corner show only on the front, while the shaded side beside them is plain. Their short returns go onto the side face, in shade, so the corner turns in stone from the pavement to the cornice.
items.code: courtHouse(), after line 1199: let qret = ''; for (let k = 0, y = street; y > top + Y(0.04); y -= Y(0.036), k++) { const rw = k % 2 ? Y(0.022) : Y(0.014), qh = Y(0.036) - 1.2; qret += `M${F(x1)} ${F(y)}h${F(rw)}v${F(-qh)}h${F(-rw)}Z`; } s += `<path class="isl-vstone" d="${qret}"/><path class="isl-vpshade" d="${qret}"/>`; If it reads as a ladder at 1920, shorten the returns one step.

items.title: Rows of balcony glass along the ships' decks
items.for_owner: On About, the cruise ships read as stacked pale slabs by Day. A band of dark balcony glass goes along each deck, as in your photo of the ship at the quay, and at night the lit cabins then sit in the glass.
items.code: harbour() ship(), lines 1382-1388: let glass = ''; in the decks loop: glass += `M${F(a + L*0.01)} ${F(yb - dh*0.66)}H${F(b - L*0.004)}v${F(dh*0.3)}H${F(a + L*0.01)}Z`; line 1398, in `one` right after the ${cls} path: `<path class="isl-vdark" d="${glass}" fill-opacity=".45"/>` (compare .45 with .55 by Day). No r().

items.title: Surf on the reef at the harbour mouth
items.for_owner: On For Students, add the line of white surf breaking on the reef that runs from the near slope into the harbour mouth. It is a real, recognisable feature in your day photo.
items.code: heights(), after line 508: const reef = P([[0.196, 0.597], [0.22, 0.59], [0.25, 0.585], [0.285, 0.584]]); s += `<path class="isl-vsurf" d="${line(reef)}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1.2, Y(0.006)))}"/>` + a fainter broken isl-vsurf stroke about Y(0.006) above + `<g class="isl-ydet"><path class="isl-vrockline" d="${line(reef.map(([x, y]) => [x, y + 1.5]))}" stroke-width="1"/></g>`; No blur filter. The slope (553) covers its landward end. Pair with #36.

items.title: Light columns under the dockyard's lamps and moored yachts
items.for_owner: On For Students, the dockyard's lamps, the moored yachts' masthead lights and the light at the end of the pier stand over the harbour with nothing on the water beneath them. Each gets a short, faint column of light, as the anchored yachts already have.
items.code: heights(), after line 520: const cr = rng(223); let cols = ''; for k in 0..4, t = (k + .5)/5: x = d0[0] + (d1[0] - d0[0])*t, y = d0[1] + (d1[1] - d0[1])*t + dt; cols += dashes(streakList(x, y, y + Y(0.09), cr, 0.05, 0.04), 's-vglow', 1, [0.1, 0.2, 0.35]); same for pier1 (468); s += `<g class="isl-vwin" style="--i:0" clip-path="url(#islvbayclip)">${cols}</g>` before the moored hulls. Moored loop (529-533): add a 1.2-wide islvrefl rect like line 547 at y = foot + Y(0.002), in <g class="isl-vlamps">. Keep them short and faint.

items.title: A halo round the station's lit windows, and a rim on its roof edge
items.for_owner: On General AI, the station's lit windows are hard rectangles with no glow, and its roof edge catches none of the evening light the hill beside it does. A soft warm glow goes round the windows, and a faint lit edge along the roof.
items.code: dishNet, after the isl-troof path: `<g class="isl-vwin" style="--i:0">${halo(bx + Y(0.15), bT + Y(0.065), Y(0.2), 'islvwarm')}</g>` (the softer islvwarm, centred on the window cluster) and `<path class="s-rim" d="M${F(bx - Y(0.01))} ${F(bT - Y(0.015) + 0.5)}H${F(bx + bw + Y(0.01))}" stroke-width="1" stroke-opacity=".4"/>`.

items.title: Make the guardhouse read as stone: staggered joints and quoins
items.for_owner: On Courses and Resources, the guardhouse is meant to be coursed stone but reads as timber siding. Staggered vertical joints go in, with narrow corner stones up its left corner.
items.code: telescope(), lines 955-957: for (let y = gBase, j = 0; y - Y(0.03) > gTop + Y(0.005); y -= Y(0.03), j++) { for (let x = gx0 + Y(0.06) - (j % 2)*Y(0.03); x < W; x += Y(0.06)) gc += `M${F(x)} ${F(y - Y(0.03))}v${F(Y(0.03))}`; q += rect(gx0, y - Y(0.03) + 0.6, Y(j % 2 ? 0.014 : 0.022), Y(0.03) - 1.2); } s += `<path class="isl-vstone" d="${q}" fill-opacity=".45"/>`; The joints are isl-vcourse .7, drawn before the door and window. The narrower quoins leave at least 3 px before the window.

items.title: Water hatch dense at the horizon
items.for_owner: On For Faculty & Staff, the open sea covers two thirds of the picture but has only sparse, even ripples, so it reads flat. It gets the usual ripples, dense at the horizon and sparse near the viewer, so the water recedes.
items.code: build(), after ripples(...) at line 3377: + (P.world === 'coast' ? dashes(hatchList(W, y0, H, rng(89)), 's-vrip', 1, [0.1, 0.18, 0.28]) : ''). It goes before sunWater and land, which cover it. Only curtain-bluff is affected.

items.title: Window reveals: the wall's thickness turning into each opening
items.for_owner: In the AI Literacy Pathway library, the windows look like flat holes, and the right-hand one like a picture hung on the wall. The wall's thickness will turn into each opening, with the white frames set back inside it, as in the study-hall photo.
items.code: library(), with lines 1512-1514: const ko = D/(D + 0.25), jamb = (x) => polyD([[x, wT], [vx + (x - vx)*ko, vy + (wT - vy)*ko], [vx + (x - vx)*ko, vy + (wB - vy)*ko], [x, wB]]); const jambs = jamb(wins[0]) + jamb(wins[1]) + jamb(wins[2] + ww) + jamb(wins[3] + ww); const kz = (sx0 - vx)/(bR - vx), rj = rect(sx0, along(bR, wT, sx0), 0.25*m*kz, along(bR, wB, sx0) - along(bR, wT, sx0)); append ${jambs}${rj} to the far wall's evenodd path (1512); add `<path class="isl-lsidew" d="${jambs}"/>`. Move the frames and mullions (1556) onto the recessed edge: scale the far windows' frame corners toward (vx, vy) by ko, and start the side window's frame at sx0 + 0.25*m*kz. The sills stay at the wall face. Render at 1920 and 1440.

items.title: A wall plate for the monitor's arm
items.for_owner: On Clinical Practice, the monitor's wall arm ends in mid-air on the wall. A small mounting plate goes where it meets the wall.
items.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2340, after the isl-hframe arm: `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(mx0 - Y(0.066), mT + mh*0.5 - Y(0.035), Y(0.018), Y(0.07))}"/>`. The optional monitor drop shadow (isl-tdrop rect(mx0 + Y(0.01), mT + Y(0.013), mw, mh) before line 2341) adds little.

items.title: The pen floats above the desk's back edge
items.for_owner: On Learning to Prompt, the pen floats above the desk's back edge, against the wall. It will lie on the desk top instead, in a colour that shows on the wood.
items.code: promptDesk line 2028: `M${F(nx + nW*0.66)} ${F(dTop + Y(0.026))}l${F(Y(0.2))} ${F(-Y(0.02))}l${F(Y(0.014))} ${F(Y(0.005))}l${F(-Y(0.2))} ${F(Y(0.02))}Z`, and change class isl-lbk1 -> isl-lbk2 (or isl-tiron), because isl-lbk1 is almost the desk's own colour. Optional 1-px isl-lalu clip near its far end. Check Day and Night at 1920 and 1440.

items.title: Tables stand on two legs: add the far legs
items.for_owner: In the AI Literacy Pathway library, the long study tables stand on only their two front legs, and the back legs that should show under the tabletops are missing. The back legs get drawn.
items.code: table(), line 1601: for (const z of [za + 0.06, zb - 0.06]) for (const lx of [lx0 + 0.06*m, lx1 - 0.12*m]) legs += quad(pt(lx, 0.7, z), pt(lx + 0.06*m, 0.7, z), pt(lx + 0.06*m, 0, z), pt(lx, 0, z)); The far legs come first, all in one winding, and the tabletop covers their tops. Skip the optional floor shadow.

items.title: The weather vane is drawn above the picture
items.for_owner: On Announcements, the bell tower's weather vane is drawn above the top of the picture, so only a cut-off rod and bar show at the edge. A small vane fits fully inside the frame instead, and the compass bar goes.

items.title: The lens reads as a pale ball stuck on the end of the tube
items.for_owner: On Courses and Resources, the telescope's lens is a pale ball stuck on the end of the tube, and it reads like a second small Moon. It becomes the glass seen nearly edge-on, filling the tube's mouth.
items.code: telescope(), line 982: `<ellipse class="isl-vlens" cx="${F(fx + ux*Y(0.01))}" cy="${F(fy + uy*Y(0.01))}" rx="${F(d0*0.3)}" ry="${F(d0)}" transform="rotate(${F(ang*180/Math.PI)} ${F(fx + ux*Y(0.01))} ${F(fy + uy*Y(0.01))})"/>` (rx about 3 px so it still reads; ang, ux, uy and d0 come from lines 963-966).

items.title: The notice board's little roof merges with the house roofs behind it
items.for_owner: On Announcements, the notice board's little roof merges with the house roof behind it: dark on dark in the evening, red on red by Day. It will be drawn in the board's own dark wood, so the board reads as one object.
items.code: bellTower(), line 2174: class="isl-troof" -> class="isl-lwood2" (the token exists in all five versions, layout-art.css 446-482).

items.title: Day houses stand on the pale far range
items.for_owner: On News & Events by Day, two crisp, near-sized houses sit on the pale, hazy far range and pop forward. Every coast light, and so every Day house, stays on the nearer green hills.
items.code: regatta(), line 687: const crestY = (x) => { for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { const [xa, ya] = hills[i], [xb, yb] = hills[i + 1]; if (x >= xa && x <= xb) return ya + (yb - ya)*(x - xa)/(xb - xa); } return Y(0.43); }; for (let i = 0; i < 18; i++) { const x = X(0.62 + r()*0.38), y = Y(0.54 + r()*0.055); lights[1].push([x, Math.max(y, crestY(x) + Y(0.015))]); } The r() order (x before y) is kept, so nothing else moves.

items.title: The century plant is in front of the stairs but behind the lantern on them
items.for_owner: On Step-by-Step Guides, the century plant passes in front of the stairs but behind a lantern standing on those stairs. The plant moves a little right so its flower branches clear the lantern.

items.for_owner: On Step-by-Step Guides, the scrub beside the steps shows at dusk and night as scattered dark dots, which read as pebbles. Four small shrubs replace it, set along the stairs' lower edge against the lighter stone and the lamplight.

items.title: Calendar and clock shadows fall toward the lights
items.for_owner: On This Week, every light in the room is on the right, yet the calendar's and clock's shadows fall to the right, into the lamp's glow and toward the window. Both shadows will fall down and to the left.

items.title: The right-hand wall's window has no sill
items.for_owner: In the AI Literacy Pathway library, the window on the right-hand wall has no sill, unlike the four on the far wall. It gets the same sill, drawn in perspective.

items.title: The lookout lantern's post is land-green by Day
items.for_owner: On For Students by Day, the lookout lantern's post is olive green like the land, so it reads as a twig. It gets the dark iron every other lamp post uses; the night versions do not change.
items.code: heights(), line 561: class="f-near" -> class="isl-vpost". The night versions are pixel-identical. It fits alongside #92, which regroups the lamp.

items.title: The lookout's warm halo is on before its windows light
items.for_owner: On Step-by-Step Guides, the lookout's warm glow is on from the start, while its windows stay dark until the end of the lighting sequence. The glow will come on with the windows, last.

items.title: Columns on the water under the window's hill lights
items.for_owner: In the window view shared by Clinical Practice, Committee Work and This Week, the lights on the far hills have no reflection on the water, though the boats' lights do. Each gets a short, faint column.
items.code: windowView(), after line 2211 and before the boats loop: const rl = rng(4057); for (const [lx] of lights) s += dashes(streakList(lx, y0 + 1, H, rl, 0.03, 0.025), 's-vglow', 1, [0.05, 0.1, 0.18]); Its own rng keeps the boats' streaks and the week calendar's shrubs unchanged; the wall covers everything below the sill.

items.title: The vise reads as a small window
items.for_owner: On Tool Directory, the bench vise's light screw bar crosses over its two dark jaws, so at full size it reads as a small four-paned window. The screw goes behind the jaws, and the hanging handle stays in front.
items.code: toolWall lines 1918-1920: split the isl-lalu path. Emit `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(vx + u*0.005, vT + jh*0.45, u*0.26, u*0.018)}"/>` (the screw) BEFORE the isl-tiron jaws/base path; then the jaws, the isl-tjaw strokes, and last `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(vx - u*0.005, vT + jh*0.05, u*0.016, jh*0.95)}"/>` (the handle). No rng. Look at 1920 and 1440 in Day and Night.

items.title: Hipped roofs split down the middle beside the now-uniform tower roof
items.for_owner: On the homepage, the four hipped roofs beside the tower are each split down the middle into light and dark halves. No roof seen straight on shows that, and the tower's roof lost the same split today. They become single planes to match, shown to you side by side because the change touches all four roofs.
items.code: campus(): remove roofShade (line 120) and its emit (line 188). Add a ridge rim only if the flat roofs read too flat in the comparison: the top H segment only, hidden by Day as well as Night (add its class to the Day display:none rule at layout-art.css line 155).

items.title: The evening planet sits half under the window frame
items.for_owner: On Tool Directory at night, Venus sits half under the window frame's top-left corner and reads as a screw head or a stray highlight. A planet will be drawn only where it stands clear of the window bars; the same rule covers Venus touching the frame on Learning to Prompt.
items.code: PIECES['tool-wall']: bars: (W, H) => { const f = toolFrame(W, H), t = H*0.012, tr = f.wT + (f.wB - f.wT)*0.42, mx = f.wx0 + f.ww/2; return [[f.wx0, f.wT - t, f.wx1, f.wT + t], [f.wx0, tr - t, f.wx1, tr + t], [mx - t, f.wT, mx + t, f.wB], [f.wx0 - t, f.wT, f.wx0 + t, f.wB], [f.wx1 - t, f.wT, f.wx1 + t, f.wB]]; }; build() line 3345: L.planets(vm, m, P.bars ? P.bars(W, H) : [], cls) (hits() already skips within 11 px). Add a matching bars hook for prompt-desk using #14's transom. Test with ?isl-moon= on a date when Venus is up.

items.title: The tipped hull lifts its stern out of the water
items.for_owner: On News & Events, tipping each yacht to show its lean lifts the stern slightly out of the water, opening a small wedge of water between the hull and its reflection. The hull gets seated at the waterline while the mast and sails keep their lean, shown to you as a before and after.
items.code: regatta(), yacht(), lines 697-711: hull = M(x - .5L, wl - hh) H(x + .5L) L(x + .42L, wl + .12L) H(x - .44L) Z; per yacht i: clips += `<clipPath id="islvwl${i}"><rect x="${F(x - L)}" y="${F(wl - H)}" width="${F(2*L)}" height="${F(H)}"/></clipPath>`; one = `<g clip-path="url(#islvwl${i})"><g ${g}>hull+sheer</g></g><g ${g}>mast+main+jib/spin</g>`; mirror as now (the clip flips with it; own() renames the isl ids). If the -8 degree yacht's bow reads as sinking, rotate the hull by half the heel. Then add #25's aft foam line.

items.title: The boats' reflections in the window view
items.for_owner: In the window view shared by Committee Work, This Week and Clinical Practice, the far land is reflected in the water but the anchored boats are not. Each boat gets a faint reflection.
items.code: windowView(), boats loop (2213-2219): const hd = `M${F(bx - hw)} ${F(by - Y(0.015)*k)}H${F(bx + hw)}L${F(bx + hw*0.72)} ${F(by)}H${F(bx - hw*0.78)}Z`, md = `M${F(bx)} ${F(by - Y(0.015)*k)}V${F(by - mh)}`; s += `<g transform="translate(0 ${F(2*by)}) scale(1 -1)" opacity=".18"><path class="isl-vhull" d="${hd}"/><path class="isl-vmast" d="${md}" stroke-width=".8"/></g>`; then hulls += hd; masts += md as now, so the boats draw over their reflections. items.title: Coffee in the mug, and its shaded side, so it reads by Day
items.for_owner: By Day the mug on Learning to Prompt, and the one on This Week, almost vanishes against the cream wall or calendar. Each mug shows its opening with dark coffee inside, and a soft shade on the side away from the window.
items.code: promptDesk line 2039, after the isl-lmug path: + `<ellipse class="isl-lmug" cx="${F(mx)}" cy="${F(mt)}" rx="${F(mw)}" ry="${F(Y(0.008))}"/><ellipse class="isl-lbronze" cx="${F(mx)}" cy="${F(mt + 0.5)}" rx="${F(mw*0.8)}" ry="${F(Y(0.0055))}"/><path class="isl-lredsh" d="${rect(mx + mw*0.35, mt + Y(0.008), mw*0.65, dTop - mt - Y(0.008))}"/>` (the shade starts below the rim). weekCalendar line 2285: the same, with sh for dTop and the shade rect on the left (from mx - mw).

items.for_owner: On Tools & Prompts, the estate house's roof overhangs its wall but casts no shadow, so it looks pasted on. A thin shadow goes under the eaves. A small pool of light at the lit door is optional.

items.for_owner: On Courses and Resources, the guardhouse roof sits straight on its wall with no shadow under the eave. That shadow band goes in; faint shingle lines on the roof are optional.

items.title: Pave the square in perspective, as the Way In picture does
items.for_owner: On Announcements, the square in front of the tower is green with parallel diagonal strokes, which read as grass by Day and as rain streaks at night. As an option for you: pave it in stone, with joints that recede in perspective, like the square in the Accessibility picture.
items.code: bellTower(), lines 2127-2130: s += `<path class="isl-apave" d="${rect(-2, ground, W + 4, H - ground + 2)}"/>`; let pav = ''; for (let y = ground + Y(0.035); y < H; y += Y(0.04) + (y - ground)*0.2) pav += `M-2 ${F(y)}H${F(W + 2)}`; for (let x = X(0.01); x < W; x += Y(0.09)) pav += `M${F(x)} ${F(ground)}l${F((x - W*0.5)*0.08)} ${F(H - ground)}`; s += `<path class="isl-vcourse" d="${pav}" stroke-width=".7" stroke-opacity=".5"/>`; (precedent: wayIn 2709-2713, layout-art.css 688-700). Check #16's plinth against the paving by Day.

items.title: Shore lights low along the near coast, with their columns
items.for_owner: On For Faculty & Staff, the coast is unlit at dusk and night, so the picture has no evening lights. As an option for you: 8 to 10 small warm lights low along the near shore at Carlisle Bay, some with reflections, and houses at the same spots by Day. The dark coast may be what you intended.
items.code: curtainBluff(): const rr = rng(71), pts = []; const near = L.LAND.filter((p) => p[4] > -90 && p[4] > p[2] && p[2] > -90 && v.x(p[0]) > W*0.42 && v.x(p[0]) < W - 4); for 8-10 draws: p = near[Math.floor(rr()*near.length)], yt = v.y0 - p[4]*v.ppd, yb = v.y0 - p[2]*v.ppd; pts.push([v.x(p[0]), yb - (yb - yt)*(0.08 + rr()*0.22), yb]) (low, near the water). Output makeKit(W, H).dayHouses(pts, H*0.02, 67); for half: dashes(streakList(x, yb, yb + H*0.12, rr, 0.04, 0.05), 's-vglow', 1, [0.08, 0.16, 0.3]); then one <path class="s-vlight isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:1" d="M x y h0 ..." stroke-width="1.3"/>. Render Dusk and Night at 1920 and 1440 before showing him.

items.title: Twin tower's shade stops short of its broken crown
items.for_owner: On Tools & Prompts, a hair-thin lit lip shows at the top of the roofless tower's shaded side, where the shade stops just short of the broken top. It is barely visible and worth doing only alongside the other Betty's Hope changes.
items.code: bettysHope(), line 1073: replace `L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.02))} ${F(twin.top)}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.09))} ${F(twin.top)}` with `L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.02))} ${F(twin.top + Y(0.003))}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.054))} ${F(twin.top - Y(0.008))}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.09))} ${F(twin.top)}` (matches tower()'s broken crown, line 1062).

items.title: The fort's coping turns the corner onto the outer wall
items.for_owner: On About, the fort wall's light capping stops at its corner instead of turning onto the outer wall above the water. It carries round the corner. The gain is very small, so do it only alongside other changes to this picture.
items.code: harbour(), line 1427: lineD(par.slice(0, 6)) -> lineD([...par.slice(0, 6), outer[1]]), and add stroke-linejoin="round".

patterns: Turn every corner (the Court House lesson). Wherever a shaded side face meets a course, cornice, cap or battlement drawn after the shade, that band crosses the shade lit. It happens on the Court House's own string course (#3), Way In (#11), the Betty's Hope mill cap and twin tower (#99, #114) and the lamp-steps turret (#34, #98). Check every building with a side strip for bands emitted after its shade.

Straight-on buildings show no side. Today's clock-tower ruling also applies to the bell tower's shaft shade (#35) and the split hipped roofs beside the campus tower (#79). Where a side face is kept, openings must sit mid-face, never on the edge (#34).

Gaps where sea or sky shows through: the campus portico (#1), Court House alleys (#7), bell-tower terrace (#27), lecture-hall seats (#28) and dish-net station (#46). The cheap general fix is a shaded back layer drawn first (link wall, back row, floor band, footing) rather than re-spacing, because re-spacing moves approved random layouts.

Nonzero-winding cancellation (the cruise-ship fault) recurs wherever one path mixes quads from two planes: the library carrels (#12). A scripted pass over island-vignettes.js for shared paths whose pieces have opposite signed areas and overlap would catch the rest.

Every light is a set, meaning the light, its halo and its column or pool, arriving together in the sequence. Items are missing one part: lights missing with columns present (#15), columns missing (#43, #57, #77), a visible source missing (#52, #53), a pool missing (#88, #89, #90, #91, #92), halo and lamp timing (#76, #92), and a hidden light with an orphan column (#13).

Lights must move with what carries them. Masthead lights miss the tilted rig (#5), a mast stands off the deck (#23), and a masthead sits on the horizon (#29). When a rig is rotated or moved, push its light points through the same transform.

Reflections under every hull: lamp steps (#94), prompt desk (#43), Curtain Bluff Day yachts (#102), and the shared window view (#82). The shared helpers windowView and windowWall carry one fix into three rooms at once (#77, #82, #87).

Window bars must never cross the Sun or a planet: #14 (Dawn Sun), #44 (Sunset Sun), #80 (Venus). A per-piece keep-out list of bar boxes passed to L.planets generalises. Check every framed-window piece at Dawn and Sunset at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120.

The two oldest window pieces predate windowWall and put the reveal on the jamb the viewer cannot see (#73, #74). Switching both to windowWall with the correct side fixes them and removes their duplicate gradient defs.
Nothing floats: the bed, drip bag and monitor arm (#10, #42, #62), pen (#63), table legs (#64), ship masts (#23), station and dish (#46, #47, #105), and bow waves and hull (#25, #81).

Per-version class leaks. A class shows in a version it was not meant for: the dusk hand at Sunset (#4), afterglow glitter at Dawn (#24). An outdoor class is used indoors (#33). A token has no Night value (#40). A shade token is still paired with a retired wall token (#2). A lamp post uses the land colour (#75). A table of which art classes display in which of the five versions would catch these mechanically.

Tone separation: an object the same tone as what is behind it disappears. Examples are the station and hill (#47), planter and wall (#48), skeleton and wall by Day (#50), mug and wall by Day (#84), notice-board roof and house roof (#67), pen and desk (#63), and plant and landscape (#33).

Keep approved compositions still. Filter points after the random draw (#8, #68), widen shapes instead of re-spacing them (#27), and give new marks their own rng stream (#43, #77, #103, #57), so an addition moves nothing the owner has already approved.
Day houses where the night lights stand, on the right depth layer: missing on Way In (#111), on the far haze at Sailing Week (#68), above the land at lamp steps (#15).
Water finish (horizon hatch, land reflection, mist at the foot of land) was skipped on some seas: #60, #101, #103.

A blur filter with the default 10% bounding-box region is cut into a box on thin or flat shapes (#17). Set filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse" with the full card box on any shared blur, and check other pieces that blur strokes.

Truth to place on the AUA campus hero: #19 (pent roof), #51 (portico gablet), #95 (lookout balustrade) and #49 (low hipped tower roof with cresting) are all from the campus photographs. Show #49 and #79 as side-by-side comparisons, since they change the focal silhouette.
ranked.dropped_summary: Eight proposals were dropped. library-5 (starting Day sun patches at the sill line): the correct physics gives only a 4 px band on an already faint patch, invisible at picture size. st-johns-harbour-4 (posts under the quay lamps): 6 px ticks that clutter the quay line by Day and vanish at night; the lights are already complete sets. telescope-2 (re-ending the footpath): the path already reads as going round the wall under the lantern, and the proposed end sits on the skyline at the water's edge. hospital-room-7 (clamping the chair away from the bed): no contact at any rendered width, and the clamp would push the chair in front of the window. way-in-2 (window lintels): they would make a striped stack under the coping and land on a rusticated joint; plain openings over sills are a normal treatment. way-in-4 (quoin returns on Way In's side face): this departs from the Court House's front-only quoins, would lighten the shade the corner depends on, and would read as a ladder. If court-house-2 (#54) is adopted, the two buildings should be reconsidered together for consistency. way-in-5 (moving the paving's vanishing point): the fan is a loose texture with no real vanishing point, the change makes the joints under the door lean harder, and its text and code disagreed. dish-net-5 (the dish's yoke): light arms on a light bowl would vanish, leaving a dark dot that reads as a blemish, and the right arm would fork off its leg. Parts were also trimmed from kept items. #1: the optional windows in the link wall. #20: moving the drive-lamp bulbs, which would make each halo appear before its lamp. #79: the roof rim light, which would show by Day as a pale line. #64: the floor shadow, which reused an unrelated class. #93: the backstay, which crosses the sail. #25: the aft foam line, which the hull covers unless #81 lands. #22: the skeleton's hands and feet, too small to read. #38: the gate piers, which have no reference, so they are an option only. #70: the proposed shrub positions, moved against the stone and clear of the agave. #17: the peak-height threshold, which would also have removed the headland's shade. #100: the rim indices, since the original ran along the water. #105: the wider plinth, which hit a shrub at 1440. #14: the 0.28 transom, which jammed the Moon. #44: the time change alone, which sank the Sun into the hill. #27: re-spacing the houses, which would shift every gable. #7: per-gap strips, which missed the sea triangles beside low roofs. #8: 32u, too tight for the house roofs. #50: the full shadow offset, which striped the ribs. #66: the 1.6 px lens, which would vanish. #91: the Day orb pool, which smeared on the wood. #109: the gradient overlay, which restretched the wall gradient. The optional monitor shadow (#62), shingle lines (#86) and door pool (#85) stay as low-value options.

proposals.title: Close the gap beside the portico where the sea shows through
proposals.observed: The portico is 11u wide (cx ± 5.5u) and the inner blocks start at cx ± 6.8u. Nothing is drawn between them, so on each side a strip about 1.3u wide (about 6.5 CSS px at 1920) runs from the portico's eave down to the lawn. The sea and its pale horizon line show through it: at Night the horizon line can be seen in the right-hand gap (3x image x≈1130, y≈1335). Above the portico roof, a notch of sky about 2.3u wide shows between each inner block's wall and the tower, down from the eave. Of the owner's catches, this is the 'gap where the sea shows through'.
proposals.proposal: Draw a recessed link wall behind the tower, portico and inner blocks. It fills both gaps from just under the inner blocks' eaves down to the lawn, in the campus shade tone (see campus-hero-2), so it reads as a set-back wall rather than as sky. Optionally, give each side one small dark window in line with the top row of the inner blocks.
proposals.why: On the real campus the tower meets each inner block through a walled section with windows, and no sky or sea shows between them. A see-through sliver next to the entrance is the same kind of fault as the cruise ship's wedge, and it sits right beside the focal tower.
proposals.code: campus(), before line 184 (the first `s += isl-vwall`): `const link = rect(cx - 6.9 * u, iTop + 0.5 * u, 13.8 * u, base - iTop - 0.5 * u); s += `<path class="isl-vshade" d="${link}"/>`;`. It is drawn first, so the walls, portico and roofs cover everything except the two gaps. Optional windows: `dark += rect(cx - 6.05 * u, iTop + 1.1 * u, 0.8 * u, 1.8 * u) + rect(cx + 5.25 * u, iTop + 1.1 * u, 0.8 * u, 1.8 * u);` (these clear the portico roof, whose slope is at about base - 8.5u there). Needs the corrected --isl-vshade from campus-hero-2; without it the link reads lighter than the walls at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-2 (straight-on view: walled, windowed sections join the tower base to both inner blocks, with no view through), aua-campus-6

proposals.title: The campus 'shade' is lighter than its walls at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk (inverted); Night (almost no contrast); Day correct
proposals.observed: The outer wings' end walls (the `shade` rect, line 128) are drawn in isl-vshade. The walls, however, are filled from --isl-vwallc (layout-art.css line 838 overrides line 769): #6d6a63 at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk, and #2b3038 at Night. --isl-vshade still carries the values that were paired with the old --isl-vwall (#707d8e at line 762, #253449 at line 766). So at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk the 'shaded' ends are pale blue-grey strips about a third lighter than the fronts, and at Night they barely differ. Only by Day (#d3c4a6 against #efe5cf) do they read as shade.
proposals.proposal: Re-pair the shade token with the wall tone it now sits against: a warm grey a step darker than #6d6a63 at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk (for example #55524d), and one darker than #2b3038 at Night (for example #20242b). Day is unchanged.
proposals.why: A face in shade that is lighter than the lit face beside it reads as light from the wrong side. It also differs between versions, when only the light should change. The recessed link in campus-hero-1 needs a true shade too.
proposals.code: layout-art.css line 762: `--isl-vshade: #707d8e` → `#55524d`; line 766: `--isl-vshade: #253449` → `#20242b`. A grep shows isl-vshade is used only by campus() (island-vignettes.js line 185), so no other picture changes. Check the hero at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk afterwards.
proposals.truth_to_place: not a real-place claim (a colour-token pairing); the drawing's own intent is the shaded end wall at line 128

proposals.title: The red pent roof across each inner block
proposals.observed: Each three-storey inner block shows its hipped roof, two rows of windows with thin rails, and the terracotta ground floor. Between the top two rows of windows there is only a thin grey rail (line 143, at iTop + 3.5u).
proposals.proposal: Add a narrow red pent roof across each inner block between the third-floor and second-floor windows. It slopes out from about iTop + 3.3u to an eave at iTop + 4.5u, overhangs each end by about 0.6u, and uses the roof red. Drop the rail at iTop + 3.5u, which it replaces, and keep the one at iTop + 7.6u.
proposals.why: The red band between the upper floors is one of the campus's signature features: every front photograph shows it on both inner blocks, and it lines up with the portico roof into a continuous red course. It is the same kind of addition as the Court House corner, a true detail carried across the facade. At 1920 it is about 6 CSS px tall.
proposals.code: campus(), inner-block loop (lines 139-151): `roofs += `M${F(x0 - 0.6 * u)} ${F(iTop + 4.5 * u)}L${F(x0 + 0.2 * u)} ${F(iTop + 3.3 * u)}H${F(x1 - 0.2 * u)}L${F(x1 + 0.6 * u)} ${F(iTop + 4.5 * u)}Z`;`. This is the same M-L-H-L-Z form and winding as block()'s roofs at line 118, so nothing cancels inside the shared `roofs` path. Line 143: keep only the `iTop + 7.6 * u` rail segment. The pent roof clears both window rows (1.1 to 2.9u and 5.2 to 7.0u) and the portico roof.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-2 (red band between the upper two floors of both inner blocks, about y 785-805), aua-campus-3 (aerial, the pent roof wraps the inner blocks), aua-campus-6

proposals.title: Drive lamps: heads by Day, pools on the lawn at night
proposals.versions: Day (bare poles); Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (no pool)
proposals.observed: The four lamp posts (postsD, line 221) are drawn in every version, but both lamp circles (the f-pulse bulbs and the kind-hue isl-vlamp) sit inside `<g class="isl-vlamps">` (line 230), which layout-art.css line 155 hides by Day. By Day, therefore, four bare dark sticks stand in front of the outer wings' arcades with nothing on top, and read as downpipes. The rule that makes a lamp unlit glass by Day (layout-art.css line 758) never reaches them. In the lit versions each lamp has its halo but no pool of light on the lawn.
proposals.proposal: Give each post a lamp in every version: a small dark cap over the globe, and the globe itself outside the hidden group, as unlit glass by Day that warms in the pass like the windows. In the lit versions, lay a small warm pool on the lawn at each post's foot.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.4: every light is a set (the light, its halo, and its pool on the ground). By Day a lamp should still look like a lamp; every other piece keeps its lantern heads by Day as isl-vpost or isl-vlamp. The real drive's posts carry lamp heads.
proposals.code: campus(), lamps.forEach (lines 219-229). (1) Add to postsD: `M${F(lx - 0.8 * u)} ${F(ly - lampH - 0.45 * u)}L${F(lx)} ${F(ly - lampH - 1.1 * u)}L${F(lx + 0.8 * u)} ${F(ly - lampH - 0.45 * u)}Z`. (2) Move the two lamp circles out of `glows` into a new `heads` string emitted after the isl-vlamps group, with `class="f-pulse isl-vwin" style="--i:9"`, or `class="isl-vlamp isl-vwin" style="--i:9"` for i === 1 (layout-art.css 956/968 animate them from --isl-vdark to lit; 964 stills them by Day). (3) Add `pool(lx, ly + 0.4 * u, 3.2 * u, 0.8 * u, 0.8)` to `glows`, so it hides by Day and fades in with the halos. pool() is at line 643 and islvpool is in extraDefs(), which heroScene already includes. In the hero ly = base, so the pool sits on the roughly 10 px lawn strip.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-1 and aua-campus-3 (the drive's lamp posts carry lamp heads)

proposals.title: A ledge and low balustrade at the foot of the lookout
proposals.observed: The lookout's glow and its seven posts end directly on the shaft at shaftTop. The top of the lookout has a projecting cornice (line 157), but its foot has no sill, so it reads as a lit slot cut into the tower rather than an open gallery.
proposals.proposal: Add a projecting ledge at the lookout's foot, slightly wider than the shaft, like the cornice above. Just above it, add a low rail across the posts, in the wall's cream, standing in front of the glow.
proposals.why: The real tower's open lookout stands on a white balustrade band, and the drive-side photographs show it. A ledge below the lookout, matching the cornice above, frames it as a gallery, much as the Court House's cornice was carried round its corner. The ledge is about 3 CSS px and the rail about 1.8 px at 1920.
proposals.code: campus(), after line 160: `posts += rect(tx0 - 0.4 * u, shaftTop - 0.25 * u, tw + 0.8 * u, 0.65 * u) + rect(tx0, shaftTop - 1.4 * u, tw, Math.max(1, 0.35 * u));`. `posts` is drawn after the lookout glow (line 193), so both stand in front of it. Every part comes from rect(), so the path has one winding.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-2 (white balustrade band under the lookout's posts, above the lettering), aua-campus-6 (ledge under the lookout)

proposals.title: The white-trimmed gablet in the portico roof
proposals.observed: The portico's roof is a plain red triangle (line 180) over the arched entrance.
proposals.proposal: Add the small white gablet the real portico has at the centre of its red roof: a cream triangle about 3.4u wide and 1.2u tall standing on the roof's eave line, with a smaller triangle inset inside it in the darker roof red.
proposals.why: This centre gablet is the portico's one distinguishing mark in every front photograph. It ties the drawing to AUA's entrance at a glance and repeats the cream trim of the walls. It is about 17 by 6 CSS px at 1920.
proposals.code: campus(), after line 187 (the isl-vroof path): `s += `<path class="isl-vwall" d="${polyD([[cx - 1.7 * u, pTop + 0.15 * u], [cx, pTop - 1.05 * u], [cx + 1.7 * u, pTop + 0.15 * u]])}"/><path class="isl-vroof2" d="${polyD([[cx - 1.15 * u, pTop - 0.05 * u], [cx, pTop - 0.75 * u], [cx + 1.15 * u, pTop - 0.05 * u]])}"/>`;` (polyD is at line 896). It sits inside the roof triangle, whose apex is at pTop - 2.6u, and above the door arch.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-2 (white triangle in the portico's red roof, about x 1000-1030, y 738-755), aua-campus-6 (white-trimmed gable at the centre of the portico roof)

proposals.title: Hipped roofs split down the middle, next to the now-uniform tower roof
proposals.observed: block() (line 120) shades each hipped roof from its vertical centre line to the right-hand eave in isl-vroof2 (line 188). Each of the four roofs therefore has a vertical edge down its middle, which would be a ridge running toward the viewer; a hipped roof seen straight on has none. Today's tower fix removed the same kind of darker half from the tower roof, so the tower is now one plane while its four neighbours are still split.
proposals.proposal: Drop the vertical half-shade. Model the roofs from real edges instead: a thin rim of light along each roof's ridge and down its left (western) hip, which face the afterglow. The rim shows at Dawn, Day, Sunset and Dusk and is hidden at Night, as every crest's rim is.
proposals.why: This follows the owner's rule from the tower (a building meant to be seen straight on shows no side at all) and the rule that lit and shaded planes must follow real faces. The rim keeps the roofs from going flat in the lit versions. The change touches all four roofs, so it is the one to show him side by side.
proposals.code: campus(): remove line 120 (roofShade) and line 188. In block() add `rims += `M${F(x0 - over)} ${F(wallTop + 0.5)}L${F(x0 + hip)} ${F(wallTop - roofH)}H${F(x1 - hip)}`;`, and for the tower roof the left slope from (tx0 - 1.4u, shaftTop - lookH - 0.8u) to the apex. After line 187 emit `<path class="s-rim" d="${rims}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1, 0.22 * u))}" stroke-opacity=".45"/>`, following the pattern at line 776. layout-art.css lines 77-78 already hide s-rim at Night.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-campus-2 (straight on, each hipped roof reads as one red plane)

proposals.title: The carrel row's nearest corner post and rails are see-through (winding)
proposals.observed: At the carrel row's near corner (X(0.78)), the aluminium corner post shows only as a hollow outline from the top rail to the floor (3x image x≈738-748), while the far-right post is solid. The end panel's top rail is also hollow for about four fifths of its length from the corner (x≈740-962, then solid to the right post), and so is a small square of the mid rail at the corner.
proposals.proposal: Wind the end-panel pieces the same way as the long-side pieces, so the overlapping post, top rail and mid rail at the corner fill solid.
proposals.why: This is the same fault as today's cruise ship. The `alu` path (lines 1703-1712) mixes quads in the long side's plane (lines 1703, 1706, 1708), which have positive signed area, with quads in the end panel's plane (lines 1704, 1712), which have negative signed area. At the corner, the long side's post (z 6.57 to 6.63) and the end panel's post (lc ± 0.03m) project onto almost the same pixels. The end panel's top rail likewise overlaps the z = 6.6 divider top (lc to lc + 1.1m). Under the default nonzero fill (isl-lalu sets no fill-rule), opposite windings cancel and the wall shows through the nearest, most prominent post of the row.
proposals.code: library(), line 1704: `quad(pt(lc, 1.42, 6.6), pt(lc, 1.47, 6.6), pt(lc1, 1.47, 6.6), pt(lc1, 1.42, 6.6)) + quad(pt(lc, 0.76, 6.6), pt(lc, 0.8, 6.6), pt(lc1, 0.8, 6.6), pt(lc1, 0.76, 6.6))`. Line 1712: `quad(pt(x - 0.03 * m, 0, 6.6), pt(x - 0.03 * m, 1.47, 6.6), pt(x + 0.03 * m, 1.47, 6.6), pt(x + 0.03 * m, 0, 6.6))`. Alternatively, emit those two lines in their own `<path class="isl-lalu">`. The end red and grey panels (1701-1702) and the end sign (1711) are also opposite-wound to their long-side neighbours but do not overlap them, so they are harmless.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-library-3-about-banner (the carrels' aluminium corner posts are solid)

proposals.title: Tables stand on two legs: add the far legs (and a soft shadow beneath)
proposals.observed: table() (lines 1597-1604) draws legs only at the near corners (z = zb - 0.06). From the camera's 1.83 m eye height, the far legs should show under the tabletop between the apron and the floor. Under far table 1 that is about 21 CSS px of leg (3x image x≈207 and x≈679, beside the near legs at 150 and 652). Under the middle table they should appear at about X(0.07). Instead only floor and chair legs show there. Nothing on the floor grounds the tables.
proposals.proposal: Draw the far pair of legs as well, behind the near ones and in the same dark wood. Optionally lay a faint shadow on the floor under each tabletop's footprint.
proposals.why: In the study-hall photograph the cherry tables stand on four legs, with the far legs plainly visible under the tops and the floor darker beneath. A long table on its two front legs floats a little, which is the 'nothing floating' caution for interiors drawn through one camera.
proposals.code: table(), line 1601: wrap the loop as `for (const z of [za + 0.06, zb - 0.06]) for (const lx of [lx0 + 0.06 * m, lx1 - 0.12 * m]) legs += quad(pt(lx, 0.7, z), pt(lx + 0.06 * m, 0.7, z), pt(lx + 0.06 * m, 0, z), pt(lx, 0, z));`. Far legs come first; all are in one path with one winding, and the tabletop, drawn after, covers their tops. Optional shadow, prepended to the returned string: `<path class="isl-lredsh" d="${quad(pt(lx0, 0, za), pt(lx1, 0, za), pt(lx1, 0, zb), pt(lx0, 0, zb))}"/>` (var(--isl-lside) at 0.12). The near table's far legs fall below the picture, which is harmless.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-library-1-study-hall-dusk (left table: near legs at about x 65-90, far leg visible at about x 230-250 under the top)

proposals.title: Window reveals: the wall's thickness turning into each opening
proposals.observed: All five windows are drawn as flat holes with their frames on the wall's face. The right-hand wall's window reads like a picture hung on the shaded side wall, with no depth.
proposals.proposal: Draw the side of each opening that faces the camera, the wall's thickness (about 0.25 m) seen in true perspective. On the right-hand wall's window this is its far jamb, a strip about 9 CSS px wide down the left of the opening. It faces the viewer as the far wall does, so it takes the far wall's lighter tone against the shaded side wall. On the far wall, windows left of the vanishing point show their left jamb and windows right of it their right jamb, about 5-6 px on the outer two and 2-3 px on the inner two. They face sideways like the side walls, so they take the side-wall shade.
proposals.why: This is the library's version of the Court House corner: a face carried round an edge, which turns flat openings into windows in a real wall. The study-hall photograph shows the windows set back in the wall with visible returns. The strips come from the same camera (D = 12), so they agree with everything else in the room. The head and sill returns work out under 1.2 px and are left out.
proposals.code: library(), with lines 1512-1514. `const ko = D / (D + 0.25), jamb = (x) => polyD([[x, wT], [vx + (x - vx) * ko, vy + (wT - vy) * ko], [vx + (x - vx) * ko, vy + (wB - vy) * ko], [x, wB]]); const jambs = jamb(wins[0]) + jamb(wins[1]) + jamb(wins[2] + ww) + jamb(wins[3] + ww); const kz = (sx0 - vx) / (bR - vx), rj = rect(sx0, along(bR, wT, sx0), 0.25 * m * kz, along(bR, wB, sx0) - along(bR, wT, sx0));`. Append `${jambs}${rj}` to the far wall's evenodd path at line 1512: inside a window hole the count is 3, so they fill again in exactly the wall gradient. Then add `<path class="isl-lsidew" d="${jambs}"/>` so the sideways-facing jambs take the side walls' shade and the side window's far jamb stays lighter. The frames (line 1556) stay on top. The Moon's pane (window 2, middle) is not covered.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-library-1-study-hall-dusk (windows set into the wall with visible returns beside their white frames)

proposals.title: The right-hand wall's window has no sill
proposals.observed: Each of the four far-wall windows has a pale sill a little wider than its frame (line 1552). The right-hand wall's window (rwin, lines 1488-1489) has only its frame and one mullion, and its bottom edge ends bare.
proposals.proposal: Give the side window the same sill, drawn in perspective along its bottom edge: slightly longer than the frame at each end, and thicker toward the viewer as the wall recedes.
proposals.why: Windows of one hall should share one detail. The missing sill makes the side window read as a different kind of opening from the four it is meant to match. It is about 2-3 CSS px thick at 1920.
proposals.code: library(), before line 1556: `const kx = (x) => (x - vx) / (bR - vx), sa = sx0 - m * 0.08 * kx(sx0), sb = sx1 + m * 0.08 * kx(sx1); sill += polyD([[sa, along(bR, wB, sa)], [sb, along(bR, wB, sb)], [sb, along(bR, wB, sb) + m * 0.07 * kx(sb)], [sa, along(bR, wB, sa) + m * 0.07 * kx(sa)]]);`. It has the same winding as the far sills' rect() and does not overlap them.
proposals.truth_to_place: aua-library-1-study-hall-dusk (the right-hand windows match the far ones)

proposals.title: Day's sun patches start at the wall's foot, below the windows' sills
proposals.observed: The sunlight on the floor (line 1559) runs from z = 0.12, right at the skirting under each window, out to z = 3.4. The window bottoms, however, are 0.62 m above the floor (wB). The patch's lateral shift also does not go to zero at the wall.
proposals.proposal: Start each patch where light through the window's bottom edge actually lands. If light through the top edge (2.5 m) lands at z = 3.4, then light through the bottom edge lands at z ≈ 0.84, shifted 0.4 m instead of 1.6 m. That leaves a band of floor in shade between the skirting and the sunlight, about 4 CSS px at 1920.
proposals.why: The light should agree with the windows it comes through. A patch touching the wall's foot implies windows that reach the floor, and the thin shaded band under each window is what real sunlight through a raised sill leaves.
proposals.code: library(), line 1559: `sun += quad(pt(x - m * 0.4, 0, 0.84), pt(x + ww - m * 0.4, 0, 0.84), pt(x + ww - m * 1.6, 0, 3.4), pt(x - m * 1.6, 0, 3.4));` (0.84 = 3.4 × 0.62 / 2.5, and the shift scales by the same ratio).
proposals.truth_to_place: not a real-place claim (light geometry from the drawing's own windows)

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The gaps show clearly as a blue strip of sea at Day (3x right half, x 1122-1143 below the portico eave), both in the 1920 render and the 1440 whole render. The pale horizon tick shows in the gap at Night and Dusk. A notch of sky also shows between the tower and each inner block above the portico roof (x 1107-1143, y 1218-1290). The geometry matches the code: portico cx±5.5u (line 178), inner blocks from cx±6.8u (line 140), tower cx±4.5u. aua-campus-2, -3 and -6 all show the inner blocks joined to the tower and portico with nothing seen through, so this is a true 'gap where the sea shows through'. The rect drawn before the walls is covered everywhere except the two gaps and fills them in one winding. Leave out the optional windows: a plain recessed strip 2.3u wide reads cleanly, and small windows in it would clutter the area beside the focal tower. It depends on campus-hero-2's shade tone, as the proposal says.

Confirmed in both code and renders. .isl-vwall is filled from --isl-vwallc (line 838 overrides 769): #6d6a63 at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk, and #2b3038 at Night. --isl-vshade is still #707d8e (line 762) and #253449 (line 766). At Dusk the outer wings' far end walls show as pale blue-grey strips (3x right half, x≈1762-1787), lighter than the fronts, and the same shows at Dawn in the whole render. Grep finds isl-vshade only at island-vignettes.js line 185, and campus() is used only by the hero (art_slots.yaml), so no other picture changes. It is a light-from-the-wrong-side error, and campus-hero-1 needs it.

True to the place and a signature feature. aua-campus-6 shows the red pent roof between the top and middle floors of both inner blocks (y≈380-420), and so do aua-campus-2 (y≈785-805) and aua-campus-3 (it wraps the blocks). The drawing has only a thin grey rail there (line 143, iTop+3.5u). The path uses the same M-L-H-L-Z form and clockwise winding as block()'s roofs, so nothing cancels. At base-10.3u to -9.1u it clears the portico roof (whose edge at cx±6.2u sits at base-8.25u). Its outer end merges into the outer wing's roof, which is how the photographs show the course meeting the wing. The clearances to the window rows are tight (0.4u and 0.7u, about 2 and 3.5 CSS px), so check it at 1440. This is the kind of 'true detail carried across the facade' the owner praised.

The observation holds. By Day the four posts (postsD, line 221) are bare dark sticks in front of the arcades (3x Day right half, x≈430, 632, 1446, 1649), because both lamp circles sit inside <g class="isl-vlamps">, which line 155 hides by Day. That goes against DESIGN 19.4 ('unlit lamps are simply there'), and it also means line 758's Day rule never reaches the kind-hue lamp. The proposed move is flawed, though. Taking the bulbs out of the group and giving them isl-vwin --i:9 lights them at 1.1+9×0.2 = 2.9 s, while their halos (still in isl-vlamps) fade in at 1.4 s, so each halo would appear before its lamp. Also, .isl-vlamp is not in the isl-vlit rule (line 956), so it would fade from 0.12 opacity rather than warm from dark glass. The pool is fine but hardly shows on the roughly 10 px lawn.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Leave the lit bulbs and halos where they are, so the pass is unchanged. (1) Add the proposed cap to postsD, so a lamp head shows in every version. (2) Add a Day-only unlit head: after line 230, `s += `<g class="isl-ydet"><path class="isl-vdark" d="${heads}"/></g>``, where heads collects, for each post, a circle at (lx, ly - lampH) of radius 0.6u (0.75u for i === 1) written as two arcs. isl-ydet shows only by Day (layout-art.css lines 158-159), and the hero root carries the class 'isl'. (3) Optionally add `pool(lx, ly + 0.3 * u, 2.6 * u, 0.6 * u, 0.6)` to glows, then check that it does not wash over the foot of the arcade.

verdicts.reason: The render confirms the lookout's posts end directly on the shaft, with no sill. aua-campus-2 and -6 show a pale rail or band at the foot of the open lookout. Both rects go into `posts`, which is drawn after the lookout glow (line 193), with one winding. The effect is small: a ledge of about 3 px and a rail of about 1.8 px. It frames the lookout as a gallery, like the cornice above, without cluttering it.

True to the place. aua-campus-6 shows a prominent white-trimmed gablet at the centre of the portico's red roof (x≈555-615, y≈330-355), and aua-campus-2 shows it too. The drawing's portico roof is a plain red triangle (line 180). The gablet fits inside the roof triangle (the roof at cx±1.7u is at pTop-1.79u) and above the door arch. At about 17×6 CSS px it reads at Day and ties the entrance to AUA. In the photographs it sits a little higher in the roof than the eave line, so its base could be raised by about 0.3u. At Night it will nearly vanish (a #2b3038 trim on a dark roof), which is acceptable.

The observation is correct: the roofShade polygon (line 120) is the right half of each front trapezoid, split at the block's centre line. In a straight-on elevation only the front plane of a hipped roof shows, since the hip ends are edge-on, so the split matches no real face. Today's tower fix removed the same fault from the tower's roof, so the neighbours are now inconsistent with it. The rim-light replacement is the weak part. s-rim shows by Day (it is hidden only at Night, lines 77-78), so a pale #f3efdf line would run along every ridge by Day. It is also a new effect on all four roofs, which the owner has not asked for.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Remove the half-shade only (line 120's roofShade, and line 188), so the four hipped roofs match the tower's single plane. Show it to the owner side by side, because it changes all four roofs. Add a ridge rim only if the flat roofs read too flat in that comparison. In that case keep it to the ridge line (the top H segment), and hide it by Day as well as Night, for example by adding its class to the Day display:none rule at layout-art.css line 155.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. In the Night 3x right half, the carrel row's nearest corner post shows only as a hollow double outline from the rail to the floor (x≈738-748). The end panel's top rail is hollow from x≈740 to ≈962 and solid only from there to the right post, which is 1.1/1.4 of its length, exactly where the divider top at z = 6.6 (line 1708) overlaps it. The fault is visible even in the Dusk whole render at 2x. I checked the winding on screen. Line 1708's quads and line 1706's posts run clockwise, while line 1704's rails and line 1712's posts run counter-clockwise, so under nonzero fill they cancel where they overlap. The proposed reorders make all four clockwise. Emitting lines 1704 and 1712 in their own <path class="isl-lalu"> is the more robust choice. It is the same fault as the cruise ship, on the nearest post of the most prominent object.

The geometry holds. From the 1.83 m eye (yF-vy = 0.28Hs = 1.826m), the middle table's far legs show from vy+2.05m (under the apron) to vy+2.96m, about 28 CSS px. The far row's show for about 21 px. table() draws only the near pair (line 1601), and the renders show only floor and chair legs where the far legs should be. The far legs' tops fall inside the tabletop quad, so the tabletop covers them. They sit in front of the far-side chairs, which are drawn earlier. The near table's far legs fall below the picture, which is harmless. It is a modest gain, since the near legs already hold the tables up. Leave out the optional shadow: reusing isl-lredsh, the carrels' shading class, for a floor shadow is a hack, and it adds a tone the owner has not reviewed.

The geometry checks out. ko = 12/12.25 gives strips of about 5 and 6 px on the outer far windows, about 2-3 px on the inner two, and about 9 px on the side window's far jamb. The heads and sills come out under 1 px. The evenodd trick works: a jamb inside a hole has a count of 3, and rj lies outside the far-wall rect with a count of 1. The Moon's pane (the centre of wins[1]) stays clear. aua-library-1 shows the returns, and on the right-hand wall's window it shows a deep one. The one problem: in the photograph the reveal lies OUTSIDE the white frame, because the frame sits back in the opening. The proposal keeps the frames (line 1556) at the wall face, so the wall-toned strip would sit inside the frame and could read as a thick frame rather than a reveal. Also, isl-lsidew is only 10-18% opacity (layout-art.css 492-493), so the jambs' tone differs only slightly from the wall's. The strip replacing the view is what will read.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Draw the jambs as proposed, and move each window's frame and mullions onto the recessed edge. For the far windows, scale the frame rect's corners toward (vx, vy) by ko. For the side window, start its frame at sx0 + 0.25·m·kz. The reveal then sits between the wall face and the frame, as in aua-library-1. Keep the sills at the wall face. Render at 1920 and 1440 to confirm the side window's 9 px return reads as wall depth.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The four far windows have pale sills a little wider than their frames (line 1552, visible in the Day renders). The right-hand wall's window (rwin, lines 1488-1489) ends in a bare frame edge. The polyD runs clockwise like rect(), and it overlaps nothing. The perspective is approximate, but at 2-3 px the difference cannot be seen. It is a small consistency fix on the nearest window.

The physics is right: the bottom-edge light lands at z ≈ 0.84 m, not 0.12 m. The visible change, though, is a band of about 4 CSS px between the skirting and a patch drawn at 40% opacity of near-white (#fffcf2) on a pale floor, and in the Day render the patches are already barely visible. The owner would not see an improvement at the picture's size, and the patch would lose part of what little presence it has.

proposals.title: Day blurs cut into boxes; flank shade spills off the land
proposals.versions: Day only (all the affected shapes are isl-ydet)
proposals.observed: Left of Galleon Beach's sand, the pale shallows are a box with a straight vertical left edge (whole Day image about x 0.745, y 0.58 to 0.66). Above the range's left slope the sky has a grey haze with a flat top (whole Day 0.42 to 0.6, y 0.2 to 0.26; clearer at 1440). The headland's shade darkens the bay water below its shore, ending in a hard horizontal line near y 0.47, plus a dark triangle on the open sea left of the cliff tip. The two small bumps on the range get narrow vertical shade wedges that read as light shafts (about x 0.61 and 0.8).
proposals.proposal: (a) Measure the blur filter in the card's own space so no blur is cut: filterUnits userSpaceOnUse, x 0, y 0, width W, height H. (b) Clip each flank's shade to its own landform, so the blur stays on the hill and never reaches sky or water. (c) Shade only real flanks: skip a peak that rises less than about 3% of the height above its valley.
proposals.why: The filter region is 10% around each shape's bounding box. On a flat shape (the beach shallows stroke, the seagrass, the dry grass, the flanks) the blur is cut off in straight lines, which shows as a box. The flanks' polygons also run below the headland's shore to Yp(0.42) and above the range's crest, so shade falls on water and sky. The owner's rule is that lit and shaded planes follow real faces of the form, or they read as stray patches.
proposals.code: heights(), line 400: <filter id="islvbayf" filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x="0" y="0" width="${F(W)}" height="${F(H)}">. Line 426: s += `<clipPath id="islvrangec"><path d="${poly(range)}"/></clipPath><g class="isl-ydet" clip-path="url(#islvrangec)">${flanks(range.slice(0, -1), Yp(0.28))}</g>`. Line 484: move flanks(head.slice(0, 18), Yp(0.42)) into its own <g class="isl-ydet" clip-path="url(#islvheadc)">, with the clipPath on poly(head); the rock, strata and trees stay in the existing group. makeKit flanks(), lines 306 to 309: after the while loop, add if (crest[j][1] - y < Y(0.03)) continue; (only heights() calls flanks). The range's minor peaks rise 0.023H and 0.008H; the main peak rises 0.136H and the headland 0.10H, so both stay.
