proposals.title: A pale vertical curtain across the harbour mouth
proposals.versions: All five (strongest at Dawn, Sunset and Night; by Day a turquoise wall)
proposals.observed: The lighter harbour water ends in a soft, straight vertical band. It hangs from the cliff tip at x 0.19 straight down to the near slope (y 0.43 to 0.63), like a beam of light standing in the open sea.
proposals.proposal: Make the harbour's lighter water start inside the mouth and meet the open sea on a diagonal from shore to shore. Move the bay polygon's first vertex from the cliff tip [0.19, 0.37] to the headland's shore just inside it, [0.235, 0.39]. The mouth edge then runs from there down-left to [0.2, 0.62] under the slope's point, and the existing blur softens it. An alternative is a mask with a horizontal gradient from x 0.18 (clear) to 0.27 (opaque) on the bay path.
proposals.why: The bay polygon's closing edge [0.2, 0.62] to [0.19, 0.37] is vertical, so its blurred edge reads as a curtain rather than as water. In every photograph the harbour's colour meets the deep sea along a soft diagonal from inside the headland's point down to the near shore.
proposals.code: heights(), line 384: const bay = P([[0.235, 0.39], [0.3, 0.4], [0.45, 0.41], ... [0.2, 0.62]]). Only the first vertex changes. islvbayclip (line 416, the Sun's path on the harbour at x 0.42 to 0.47) is unaffected, as are the Day shallows, which follow the shores.
proposals.truth_to_place: web-shirley-heights-day-panorama and shirley-heights-1: the turquoise harbour water shades into the deep blue diagonally from the headland's foot toward the near-left shore, with no vertical line. shirley-heights-7-owner-day shows the same.

proposals.title: The lookout lantern: a pool of light, and last in the pass
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (by Day the lamp is unlit glass and the pool gradient is clear)
proposals.observed: The lantern in the page's hue on the lookout's crest has a halo, but no pool of light on the ground at its foot. It is also outside the one pass: it is lit from the first frame while the dockyard, boats, Falmouth and the slopes come on in turn, and the slopes' group carries isl-vlast.
proposals.proposal: Lay a small warm pool on the slope at the post's foot. Put the lantern's halo, pool and lamp in a <g class="isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:8">, so the page's own light comes on last after the slopes, and drop isl-vlast from the slopes' group.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.4: every light is a set (the light, its halo and its pool or column), and the focal light comes last. The lamp-lit steps and the other lanterns already do this.
proposals.code: heights(), lines 560 to 563: keep the post path, then s += `<g class="isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:8">${pool(lx, ly + Y(0.02), Y(0.05), Y(0.011), 0.6)}<circle ... fill="url(#islvlamp)"/><circle class="isl-vlamp" .../></g>`. The pool's ry keeps it below the crest; the foot is Y(0.02) under it. Line 580: use class `s-vlight isl-vwin` for every group (remove the g === 3 isl-vlast).

proposals.title: Afterglow rim on the range's crest beside the Sun
proposals.versions: Sunset and Dusk (wrapped in isl-d; s-rim is already hidden at Night)
proposals.observed: At Sunset the Sun stands just above the junction of the distant point and the main range (x about 0.44), but the range's left slope, which faces it, is a flat navy silhouette against the orange sky. Sailing Week and Curtain Bluff both rim their crests; this piece has no rim.
proposals.proposal: Draw a faint s-rim along the range's crest from its left foot up to the main peak (range.slice(0, 8), offset 0.5 px down, stroke-opacity about .45). Add a fainter one (.3) on the distant point's crest nearest the Sun (point.slice(4, 8)), drawn just after the point so the range covers its right end.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3 lists a rim of afterglow along crests facing the light. This is the one crest in the picture that stands against the glow, so the rim both shapes the range and places the Sun behind it.
proposals.code: heights(): after line 427, s += `<g class="isl-d"><path class="s-rim" d="${line(range.slice(0, 8).map(([x, y]) => [x, y + 0.5]))}" stroke-width="1" stroke-opacity=".45"/></g>`. After line 421 (the point): the same for point.slice(4, 8) with stroke-width .8 and stroke-opacity .3. Rim colours come from --isl-rim: Sunset #ffcf9c by default, Dusk #c99774.
proposals.truth_to_place: shirley-heights-6-owner-dusk: the Sun sets behind this range, and its edges nearest the glow are lit.

proposals.title: Light columns under Nelson's Dockyard's dock lamps and moored yachts
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (s-vglow and isl-vlamps are hidden by Day)
proposals.observed: The five lamps along the dockyard's dock, the seven moored yachts' masthead lights and the light at the end of Galleon Beach's pier stand over the water with no reflection. The anchored yachts across the bay each lay a column.
proposals.proposal: Under each dock lamp and the pier-end light, lay a short broken column on the bay (streakList + dashes, s-vglow, about Y(0.09) long). Start it at the dock's front edge, clip it to the harbour (islvbayclip), and draw it before the moored hulls so they cover it. Give each moored yacht the same thin mast reflection the anchored ones have (a 1.2-wide rect with islvrefl, from its waterline).
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3 and 19.4 put a broken column of light on the water under every light over water. The dockyard is the first group in the pass, and its lights are the brightest in the owner's night photograph.
proposals.code: heights(), after line 520 (the dock path): const cr = rng(223); let cols = ''; for k in 0..4, u = (k + .5) / 5: x = d0[0] + (d1[0] - d0[0]) * u, y = d0[1] + (d1[1] - d0[1]) * u + dt; cols += dashes(streakList(x, y, y + Y(0.09), cr, 0.05, 0.04), 's-vglow', 1, [0.1, 0.2, 0.35]); then the same for pier1 (line 468). s += `<g class="isl-vwin" style="--i:0" clip-path="url(#islvbayclip)">${cols}</g>`. In the moored loop (lines 529 to 533) add a rect like line 547 at y = foot + Y(0.002), output in <g class="isl-vlamps">. The new rng avoids moving any other drawing.
proposals.truth_to_place: shirley-heights-3 (night view from the lookout): the dockyard's lit masts and quay lay gold columns across the water.

proposals.title: Surf on the reef at the harbour mouth
proposals.versions: All five (surf strokes; the rock line by Day only)
proposals.observed: Where the lookout's slope meets the harbour mouth (the slope's point at x 0.19, y 0.63), the water is plain. The only surf is at the headland's cliff point.
proposals.proposal: Draw a line of white surf breaking along a low reef that runs from the slope's point into the mouth: P([[0.196, 0.597], [0.22, 0.59], [0.25, 0.585], [0.285, 0.584]]), in isl-vsurf at width max(1.2, Y(0.006)), with a second, fainter broken stroke about Y(0.006) above it. By Day, add a thin isl-vrockline under it for the dark rocks. Draw it after the bay and before the slope, so the slope covers its landward end. Use no blur filter on it; a thin shape's blur is cut into a box, as in proposal 1.
proposals.why: This is a real, recognisable feature of the view, like the Court House corner: it marks the harbour's mouth. At about 70 CSS px long it reads at the picture's size.
proposals.code: heights(): after line 508 (the surf at the point), const reef = P([...]); s += `<path class="isl-vsurf" d="${line(reef)}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1.2, Y(0.006)))}"/>` + `<g class="isl-ydet"><path class="isl-vrockline" d="${line(reef.map(([x, y]) => [x, y + 1.5]))}" stroke-width="1"/></g>`. The slope polygon (line 553) is drawn later and covers the start.
proposals.truth_to_place: shirley-heights-7-owner-day, bottom left: a line of dark rocks with breaking surf runs from the near shore into the mouth. shirley-heights-1 (a grey reef shelf off the near-left shore) and web-shirley-heights-day-panorama (the same spot) show it too.

proposals.title: The caption names Montserrat, but the island drawn is Nevis
proposals.observed: The caption reads "The view from Curtain Bluff, with Montserrat on the horizon". The one island on the horizon is a small single cone at x 0.18 to 0.2, with a sliver of Redonda cut by the left edge.
proposals.proposal: Change the caption in data/art_slots.yaml (line 102) to "The view from Curtain Bluff, with Nevis on the horizon", and correct the note at lines 47 to 51: Montserrat is visible from the bluff, but not in this picture's frame. Keeping Montserrat would mean turning the view about 40 degrees further south, which moves the sunset and the coast; that is not a small change. data/art_slots.yaml is owner-owned, so quote the new label back to him before applying it.
proposals.why: The coast world anchors the sunset (293.15 degrees) at 0.3W with ppd = min(W/62, y0/29) = 7.5 at 1920 (6.2 at 1440). The frame's left edge is therefore about 261 degrees at both widths. Nevis's southern end (NEVIS_L = 280) falls at 0.18W, where the cone is drawn, and Redonda (about 261 degrees) sits at the edge. Montserrat's northern end is at 241 degrees (island-core.js, comment near line 556), 20 degrees off the left edge. Its drawn height would be about 26 px against the cone's 9 px. A reader who knows the island would see the caption contradict the picture.
proposals.code: data/art_slots.yaml line 102: caption: "The view from Curtain Bluff, with Nevis on the horizon"; update the comment at lines 47 to 51. No drawing code changes. The facts are checked against island-core.js: SKY.d.sun = [293.15, -7.02], NEVIS_L = 280, and PIECES['curtain-bluff'].ppd.
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-beach-loungers-montserrat and owner-west-beach-montserrat show Montserrat as a long island with several peaks, not the single small cone drawn here. That cone matches Nevis at its true bearing.

proposals.title: A Day yacht's sail hides Nevis
proposals.observed: The smallest yacht (fx 0.2) stands right on the horizon in front of the island at x 0.18 to 0.2, and its white sail covers the right half of the only island in the view. Because the island scales with the card, this happens at every width.
proposals.proposal: Move that yacht clear of the island, for example fx 0.2 to 0.255 (open water between the island and the low spit, still behind the sunset path). Alternatively lower it (fy 0.09 to 0.16) so its masthead stays under the horizon.
proposals.why: The island is the picture's named far feature. Hiding it by Day weakens the at-a-glance reading the owner asks for.
proposals.code: curtainBluff(), line 597: change the first entry [0.2, 0.09, 1] to [0.255, 0.09, 1] (or [0.2, 0.16, 1]).
proposals.truth_to_place: Not a place feature; composition only.

proposals.title: The coast's reflection and mist at its foot
proposals.observed: Antigua's coast (x 0.26 to 1) meets the sea along a clean hard line. There is no reflection of the hills in the water under them and no mist at their foot, where Sailing Week has both.
proposals.proposal: Mirror the coast into the water at about 0.15 opacity, without the rims. Draw it before the land in build(), so the land covers the overlap at the shoreline. Then lay a long, low mist along the coast's foot (x 0.25 to 1).
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3 puts reflections of land at the waterline and mist at the foot of the land. They are the two finishes that make the Sailing Week coast look painted rather than cut out.
proposals.code: build(), line 3379, before the coast land: + (P.world === 'coast' ? mirrored(y0, land(v, 0, W, 13, [], false), 0.15) : ''). Only curtain-bluff is a coast world. land() with seed 13 redraws the same shape, and mirrored() clips to #islsea. curtainBluff(), line 602: prepend mist(W * 0.25, v.y0 + 1, W * 0.78, H * 0.035, 0.45).
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-dickenson-bay-dusk: the far shore sits in a soft haze at the waterline, and the calm water under it is darkened by it.

proposals.title: Water hatch dense at the horizon
proposals.observed: The sea has only the core ripples: sparse dashes spread evenly, no denser toward the horizon. The open sea is two thirds of this picture and reads flat beside Sailing Week's.
proposals.proposal: Add the finish hatch (hatchList + dashes, s-vrip, alphas 0.1, 0.18 and 0.28) to the coast piece's water. Draw it before the land and before the Sun's path, so both cover it.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3 applies it to every sea: short ripples dense at the horizon, long and sparse near the viewer, so the water recedes.
proposals.code: build(), after ripples(...) at line 3377: + (P.world === 'coast' ? dashes(hatchList(W, y0, H, rng(89)), 's-vrip', 1, [0.1, 0.18, 0.28]) : ''). hatchList and dashes are declarations in the same scope. Only curtain-bluff is affected.

proposals.title: Shore lights along the near coast, with their columns
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night as lights; Day as small houses
proposals.observed: At Dusk and Night the coast is unlit, so the picture has no lights and no pass of lights. The near dark band of land (x 0.42 to 1) is the Carlisle Bay and Old Road shore.
proposals.proposal: Scatter about 14 warm lights on the near land and give about half of them a short broken column on the sea. Put them in one s-vlight path with isl-vwin isl-vlast, as Sailing Week does, and add dayHouses at the same points so a light at night is a house by Day. Place each light between the near land's top and its shoreline for its bearing, so none floats.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.4: every light is a set, and the pass tells a small story. The piece currently has no lights at all, and the owner prefers pictures that come alive in the one pass. Offer it for his decision, since the empty coast may be intended.
proposals.code: curtainBluff(): const rr = rng(71), pts = []; const near = L.LAND.filter((p) => p[4] > -90 && p[4] > p[2] && p[2] > -90 && v.x(p[0]) > W * 0.42 && v.x(p[0]) < W - 4); for 14 draws: p = near[Math.floor(rr() * near.length)], yt = v.y0 - p[4] * v.ppd, yb = v.y0 - p[2] * v.ppd; pts.push([v.x(p[0]), yb - (yb - yt) * (0.25 + rr() * 0.45), yb]). Output makeKit(W, H).dayHouses(pts, H * 0.02, 67), then columns dashes(streakList(x, yb, yb + H * 0.12, rr, 0.04, 0.05), 's-vglow', 1, [0.08, 0.16, 0.3]) for half, then <path class="s-vlight isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:1" d="M x y h0 ..." stroke-width="1.3"/>.
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-dickenson-bay-dusk: small warm lights along the far shore at dusk. The coast north-west of the bluff (Carlisle Bay, Old Road) is inhabited.

proposals.title: Reflections under the Day yachts
proposals.observed: The four Day yachts stand on the water as bare white shapes, with no reflection and no wake. Sailing Week's yachts have both.
proposals.proposal: Mirror each yacht's hull and sails about its own waterline at about 0.18 opacity, and add a short isl-vsurf wake behind the stern: they sail left, so the wake trails right, about 0.8L long at by + 1.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3 gives every hull and sail its reflection. It also sets the boats into the water rather than onto it.
proposals.code: curtainBluff(), lines 597 to 601: build const one = hull + sails; yachts += one + `<g transform="translate(0 ${F(2 * by)}) scale(1 -1)" opacity=".18">${one}</g>` + `<path class="isl-vsurf" d="M${F(bx + L * 0.4)} ${F(by + 1)}h${F(L * 0.8)}" stroke-width="1"/>`. Everything stays inside the existing isl-ydet group.
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-galleon-beach-fort-berkeley: yachts on calm water carry clear reflections.

proposals.title: Masthead and bow lights do not follow the heeled rig
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (nav lights hidden by Day)
proposals.observed: Every yacht's white masthead light hangs in open sky to the right of its mast top: about 13 CSS px on the nearest yacht, 10 px on the pink-spinnaker yacht, and visibly on all six at 1920 and 1440. The red and green bow lights sit a few px above the tipped bow.
proposals.proposal: Put the lights through the same rotation as the drawing, so the masthead light sits on the mast top and the sidelights on the bow. The yachts are drawn side-on sailing left, so the viewer sees their port side: while there, drop the green (starboard) light. Both red and green show only on a boat heading straight at the viewer.
proposals.why: The yacht is drawn inside rotate(heel, x, wl), but lights[0] is pushed at the unrotated points. A 6 to 8 degree turn about the waterline moves a masthead 1.58L up by about 0.17 to 0.19L sideways. It is the "parts that do not line up" kind of fault the owner catches first.
proposals.code: regatta(), yacht(), line 713: const a = heel * Math.PI / 180, ca = Math.cos(a), sa = Math.sin(a), rot = (px, py) => [x + (px - x) * ca - (py - wl) * sa, wl + (px - x) * sa + (py - wl) * ca]; lights[0].push([...rot(x - L * 0.5, wl - hh), 'r'], [...rot(mx, wl - hh - mh * 1.02), 'w']). Omit the 'g' push; halos (line 726) follow automatically.
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-galleon-beach-fort-berkeley shows the rigs. Sidelight visibility follows the collision regulations: red to port, green to starboard, each visible only on its own side.

proposals.title: Glitter under an empty western sky at Dawn
proposals.observed: At Dawn a column of warm gold dashes runs down the water from the horizon at x about 0.39. There is no Sun, afterglow or light above it: the western sky there is Dawn's pink band.
proposals.proposal: Show the afterglow's glitter only when the afterglow is there, at Sunset and Dusk, by adding the isl-d class to it.
proposals.why: The glitter is classed s-vglow isl-aglow, which Day and Night hide but Dawn does not. Dawn hides the afterglow itself (glowSky is isl-d or isl-n), so its reflection is left under nothing. That is light from the wrong side of the sky.
proposals.code: regatta(), line 676: 's-vglow isl-aglow' becomes 's-vglow isl-aglow isl-d'. isl-d is shown at Sunset and Dusk and hidden at Dawn, Day and Night (layout-art.css lines 70 and 118).
proposals.truth_to_place: Not a place feature; sky logic (DESIGN 19.6).

proposals.title: Bow waves float free ahead of the bows
proposals.versions: All five (by Day bright white, where they read as small gulls on the water)
proposals.observed: Each bow wave is a small white arc that starts about 0.09L ahead of where the tipped stem meets the water (7 CSS px on the nearest yacht) and curls further forward. It sits detached on the water ahead of the boat.
proposals.proposal: Start the foam where the stem meets the water, about x - 0.46L for these heels, and let it climb the stem and fall back. For example: M(x - 0.46L, wl) q(-0.05L, -0.9hh) (-0.15L, -0.1hh), plus a short foam line trailing aft along the waterline from the stem to about x - 0.25L.
proposals.why: A bow wave is water pushed up by the stem, so it touches the hull. Detached, it reads as a separate object. The fixed start matches the rotated stem, which crosses wl at about x - 0.46L for a -6 degree heel.
proposals.code: regatta(), yacht(), line 712: replace the first subpath M${F(x - L * 0.55)} ${F(wl)}q... with M${F(x - L * 0.46)} ${F(wl)}q${F(-L * 0.05)} ${F(-hh * 0.9)} ${F(-L * 0.15)} ${F(-hh * 0.1)}M${F(x - L * 0.46)} ${F(wl + 0.5)}H${F(x - L * 0.25)}. The stern wake subpaths stay.
proposals.truth_to_place: Not place-specific (how a hull makes a bow wave).

proposals.title: The tipped hull lifts its stern out of the water
proposals.observed: Each yacht, hull included, is turned 4 to 8 degrees about (x, wl). The bow dips below the waterline and the stern's underside rises about 0.04L above it (3 CSS px on the nearest yacht). Between the stern and its mirrored reflection a wedge of open water opens (about 6 CSS px), with the wake lines drawn in the gap.
proposals.proposal: Keep the lean, but seat the hull in the water. Draw the hull deeper (its bottom to about wl + 0.12L) and clip it at the waterline outside the rotation, so the rotated hull's bottom edge is the horizontal waterline along its whole length and meets its reflection. Rotate the rig as now.
proposals.why: The DESIGN caution says nothing floats. A boat pitched in the water has a horizontal waterline cutting its hull, and the reflection must touch the hull.
proposals.code: regatta(), yacht(), lines 697 to 711: hull = M(x-.5L, wl-hh) H(x+.5L) L(x+.42L, wl+.12L) H(x-.44L) Z. Per yacht i, clips += `<clipPath id="islvwl${i}"><rect x="${F(x - L)}" y="${F(wl - H)}" width="${F(2 * L)}" height="${F(H)}"/></clipPath>`. one = `<g clip-path="url(#islvwl${i})"><g ${g}>hull+sheer</g></g><g ${g}>mast+main+jib/spin</g>`. fleet += one; rf += the mirrored one (inside the mirror, the clip's user space flips, so it keeps the reflection below wl). The ids start with isl, so own() renames them.

proposals.title: The coast rim runs across the land and into the water
proposals.versions: Sunset and Dusk for the rim; Dawn, Day, Sunset and Dusk for its reflection
proposals.observed: The rim is drawn on the nearer hills' crest, which at every x lies in front of the taller far range. At Dusk it reads as a thin warm wire across dark land (x 0.6 to 1, y 0.44 to 0.6; plainer still at 1440). The land's reflection includes the rim, so a faint pale line also crosses the water diagonally from x 0.6 to the right edge.
proposals.proposal: Move the coast's rim to the far range's crest, which is the true skyline (range.slice(1, 9)), strongest nearest the Sun. Keep both rims (Montserrat's and the coast's) out of the mirrored land, so the water shows the hills' reflection but no line.
proposals.why: An afterglow rim appears only where a crest stands against the glow. A crest in front of a higher ridge is shaded by it. The owner has already removed stray lit planes from this coast (DESIGN 19.3 caution).
proposals.code: regatta(), lines 680 and 686: build the two rim paths into a separate string rims (Montserrat's unchanged; the coast's on range.slice(1, 9) with stroke-opacity .45). Line 689: s += land + regattaHouses + mirrored(y0, land, 0.18) + rims. The hills keep their shape; only the line moves.
proposals.truth_to_place: Not place-specific (backlight logic). Montserrat's rim, which is on its skyline, stays.

proposals.title: A boom under each mainsail, and a backstay
proposals.observed: Each mainsail's foot is a bare straight edge floating 0.4hh above the deck (about 3 CSS px on the nearest yacht), with sky or sea showing between sail and deck. No spar holds it, and nothing runs from the masthead to the stern.
proposals.proposal: Inside the rotated group, draw a boom along the mainsail's foot, from the mast to just past the clew (mx to mx + 0.48L at wl - 1.4hh), in the mast's own class and width. Add a hair-thin backstay from the masthead to the stern (mx, top) to (x + 0.5L, wl - hh), at about 0.6 px and 0.5 opacity.
proposals.why: Every racing mainsail is set on a boom, and a backstay is the most visible line of a racing rig. Both are details like the Court House corner: a spar where the eye expects one, so the rig reads as rigged rather than cut from paper. On the nearest yacht the boom is about 39 CSS px long.
proposals.code: regatta(), yacht(): after the main at line 707, add `<path class="isl-vmast" d="M${F(mx)} ${F(wl - hh * 1.4)}H${F(mx + L * 0.48)}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(0.8, L * 0.014))}"/>` and `<path class="isl-vmast" d="M${F(mx)} ${F(wl - hh - mh * 1.02)}L${F(x + L * 0.5)} ${F(wl - hh)}" stroke-width=".6" stroke-opacity=".5"/>`. They sit in `one`, so the reflection gets them too.
proposals.truth_to_place: owner-galleon-beach-fort-berkeley: the yachts' booms and backstays show clearly against the sky.

checked_fine: Shirley Heights: the landforms still match the owner's dusk and day photographs: headland with its cliff point, Fort Berkeley's spur, the round bay, Galleon Beach's curve, the dockyard on its land bridge, the inner harbour, Falmouth's water and its range.

Shirley Heights: the Sun at Sunset stands just above the point/range junction, its path is on the open sea and a fainter one is clipped to the harbour, and the headland covers the path where it stands between. There is no Sun at Dawn or Day.
Shirley Heights: the anchored yachts' masthead lights each lay a thin mast reflection. Their masts are vertical and their hulls sit on the water.

Shirley Heights: every house (bluff compound, dockyard, slope, beach) stands on its land with its base inside the outline, and the hip shade is on the side away from the Day Sun. The walls are drawn straight on, so no side faces are needed.
Shirley Heights: the pass runs dockyard, boats, Falmouth, slopes. By Day no light comes on, halos and pools are clear, and the lantern is unlit glass.
Shirley Heights: Dawn gilds the range's and headland's crests; Night has no rims or glow.
Shirley Heights: the Galleon Beach pier ends at the water's edge, not across the sand. The anchored hulls do not overlap. The moored hulls overlap, but share one winding, so no fill cancels.

All three pieces: every polygon sharing a path with its scrub domes (town, head, slope, range, hills) is wound clockwise, as the domes are, so no sliver of sea shows through. Every H and V command takes one number. No path in heights(), regatta() or curtainBluff() builds a NaN from its inputs (I read the code; I did not scan the rendered attributes).
Curtain Bluff: the islands are at true bearings (Redonda at the left edge, Nevis at 0.18W) at both 1920 and 1440. The afterglow rim is only on the coast's crest near the sunset and is gone at Night.

Curtain Bluff: the Sun at 18:25 sinks behind the low point, with its path on the sea. The frigatebird hangs in open sky clear of the Moon, Venus and Jupiter. Night shows the dense stars and the Milky Way. Dawn's clouds and Day's clouds stay clear of the bird.

Sailing Week: Montserrat (left) and the south coast (right) are at plausible bearings for the moonX anchor. The kind-hue spinnaker appears once. Mist lies at the coast's foot, and the coast lights lay columns that stop 0.18H down.

Sailing Week: the fleet's reflections are mirrored about each boat's own waterline and clipped to the sea, and the sail glints sit under each boat. Day hides the nav lights, halos and columns, and shows houses where the coast lights are.

Sailing Week: the Sun at Sunset touches the sea between the yachts, its path running between their reflections. Night hides the glow, the glitter and the rims. The composition keeps its shapes at 1440 (everything is sized from X()).

verdicts.reason: Real, and the worst Day fault in the three pieces. At 1440 Day the flat-topped grey haze above the range's left slope is obvious. At 1920 there is a vertical left edge on the Galleon Beach shallows (3x right half, x about 652), a hard horizontal line under the headland's shore (3x left half, y about 455), and pale shafts between the flank wedges. The cause checks out: islvbayf is 10% of each shape's bounding box, and the stroke width and blur (about 9.8 px) are not in that box. Parts (a) and (b) are right. Part (c) as written is wrong. With Y(0.03), the headland's only flank is dropped as well. Its valley [0.288,0.297] (the while loop stops at the equal 0.297 pair) to its peak [0.4,0.266] rises 0.031 x k (0.909) = 0.028H, which is under 0.03H, not the 0.10H the proposal claims. It also misses isl-vdry. That shape uses the same filter; its box is only about 20 px tall, so it is cut at top and bottom and at x 0.18W (over the cliff, onto the sea). With a full filter region it would spread onto the bay and sea unless it is clipped too.
verdicts.revised_proposal: (a) Give islvbayf filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse" x="0" y="0" width=W height=H. (b) Clip the range's flanks to poly(range). Put the headland's flanks and the dry-grass tint (line 492) in one isl-ydet group clipped to poly(head), so no blur reaches sky or water. The shallows and seagrass stay unclipped, since the land drawn later covers them. (c) Leave makeKit.flanks alone and pass only the main peak: flanks(range.slice(0, 10), Yp(0.28)). Then index 8 [0.585, 0.154] is the only peak, so the 0.645 and 0.85 wedges and the light shafts between them go, and the headland keeps its shade. Re-render Day at 1920 and 1440. Check that the Galleon Beach shallows now fade left, and do not creep up the town shore toward the dock.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in every version. At Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night (1920 and 1440) a soft vertical light band hangs from the cliff tip at x 0.19 to the slope. It comes from the bay polygon's closing edge [0.2,0.62] to [0.19,0.37]. The references support a diagonal: in shirley-heights-1 and the day panorama, the harbour colour meets the deep blue along a line from well inside the headland's point down to the reef off the near shore. The proposed vertex [0.235, 0.39] is too timid, though. At 1920 the edge would lean only about 24 degrees from vertical (26 px across 59 px), so it still reads as a leaning beam of light.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Move the bay's first vertex further into the mouth, onto the headland's shore at about [0.27, 0.397]. The mouth edge then runs about 45 degrees, from the slope's point (0.2, 0.6) up to the headland, as in shirley-heights-1. Keep the existing blur, and if the edge still reads as a line, feather it with a mask. islvbayclip changes with it, but the Sun's harbour path at x 0.42 to 0.47 stays inside. Pair it with shirley-heights-6, so the reef lies on the boundary as in the photograph.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The lantern (lines 560 to 563) is outside isl-vwin, so it is lit from the first frame. The slopes' group (line 580) carries isl-vlast. There is no pool at its foot. Every other kind-hue lamp in the art (lines 995, 1097, 2185) is a set in <g class="isl-vwin isl-vlast"> with a pool, so this follows DESIGN 19.4 and the house pattern. By Day the halo is hidden ([fill*=lamp)]), the pool clears (--isl-g1 transparent), and the vwin animation is off. The pool at ly+Y(0.02) with ry Y(0.011) stays under the crest. It is small at 1x (about 15 by 3 px), so the gain is modest.

The observation holds. At Sunset the Sun (x about 0.44) stands beside the range's left slope, which is a flat navy silhouette, while Sailing Week and Curtain Bluff rim their skylines. The owner's dusk photograph shows the edge nearest the glow only faintly lighter, so keep it faint. The indices are wrong, though. range.slice(0, 8) starts at [0.45, 0.25], which is below the horizon (Yp(0.25) = 0.318H against y0 = 0.3H), so a lit line would run along the water. It also ends at 0.56, short of the main peak [0.585, 0.154] it claims to reach. Wrapping it in isl-d is right here, since Dawn already has its own gild line on this crest (isl-adet).
verdicts.revised_proposal: Use range.slice(1, 9) (from [0.46, 0.236] up to the main peak), offset 0.5 px down, stroke-width 1, stroke-opacity about 0.4, inside <g class="isl-d">. Add the fainter point rim (point.slice(4, 8), 0.8 px at 0.3) after the point. Check at Sunset that it reads as the crest catching the glow and not as a line through the Sun's disc, and at Dusk that it stays quiet.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at Dusk (3x right half). The five dock lamps, the seven moored yachts' masthead lights and the Galleon Beach pier-end light stand over the water with nothing under them. The anchored yachts each have an islvrefl rect. The owner's night reference (shirley-heights-3) shows the dockyard's lit masts and quay laying gold on the water. That is the brightest part of the view and the first group in the pass, so this is true to the place and follows DESIGN 19.3. The code is feasible. islvbayclip is defined at line 416, before use, and the dock lies inside the bay polygon. A fresh rng(223) moves nothing else. s-vglow and isl-vlamps are hidden by Day. Keep the columns short and faint, since the dock area is only about 59 px wide at 1920.

The reef is real. shirley-heights-1 shows a grey reef shelf running from the near-left shore into the harbour mouth, the owner's own day photo (7) shows surf breaking along it at bottom left, and the panorama shows rocks at the same spot. The drawing's water there is plain. The proposed line starts at the slope's point [0.19, 0.592] and runs out over the water (above the slope's shore). At about 70 CSS px it reads at 1920, and it gives the mouth its landmark, the kind of true small addition the owner praised in the Court House corner. The existing surf at the cliff point shows the class reads in every version. Draw it without a filter, as proposed.

Verified against the data. The coast view anchors the sunset (SKY.d.sun 293.15) at 0.3W. At 1920, W = 814 and H = 311, so y0 = 218 and ppd = min(13.1, 7.5) = 7.5. The left edge is therefore 293.15 - 244.2/7.5 = 260.6 degrees. Redonda's skyline (26064 to 26178) lands at x 0 to 9 px, the sliver at the edge. Nevis (27995 to 28290) lands at 0.178W to 0.205W, which is exactly the cone drawn. Montserrat starts at 222 degrees and is entirely out of frame. The 1440 render puts the cone at the same 0.18 to 0.2. The art_slots.yaml note is itself right about the place (Montserrat lies southwest and is visible from the bluff), but not about this picture, which faces west to north. For an owner who wants landmarks true to the place, the caption contradicting the picture is a real error. Quote the new caption to him before editing the owner-owned file. Mention that keeping Montserrat would need a much wider or re-aimed frame.

Confirmed at both widths. At 1920 (3x left half) and at 1440 Day, the fx 0.2 yacht's sail covers the right half of the only island on the horizon. Once the caption names Nevis, hiding it by Day matters more. Moving it to fx 0.255 puts it on open water just short of where the low coast begins (about 0.257 at 1440), with its sail against the sky. Lowering it to fy 0.16 also works: its masthead then sits just under the horizon (mh = 14.8 px, 15 px below y0). Either is fine; check it does not crowd the fy 0.16 yacht at 0.34.

Real. At every version the coast meets the sea on a hard line, with no reflection or mist, while Sailing Week has both (DESIGN 19.3). The code is feasible. land, mirrored and mist are all in build()'s scope, and land(v, 0, W, 13, [], false) redraws the same shape without rims or underfoot. One caveat: mirroring about the horizon puts the near band's reflection a little short, because its shoreline is about 7 px below y0 at 1920. At 0.15 that will not read. Render Sunset to confirm the mirrored low spit at x 0.26 to 0.3 does not dull the Sun's path, and Day to confirm the tint is not heavy over two thirds of the sea. The mist is the safer half, if only one is taken.

Confirmed. The sea has only the core ripples, sparse and even, while Sailing Week lays hatchList over those same core ripples and its water recedes. This piece's sea is two thirds of the picture, so it gains the most. The call is feasible in build(): hatchList, dashes and rng are in scope. Placed after ripples and before sunWater and land, it is covered by both. It is limited to the coast world, so only Curtain Bluff changes.

The observation is right: at Dusk and Night the coast is unlit, and the piece has no pass of lights. The place supports it. At 1920 the near dark band covers bearings of about 306 to 9 degrees within 900 m: the Curtain Bluff resort's own shore toward Carlisle Bay, which is lit at night. The dark, empty coast under the starfield may be intended, though; it was the approved homepage view. This is medium effort, so it is for the owner's decision. Scattering lights evenly up the slope would look arbitrary. Resort and village lights sit low, near the water.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Offer it to the owner as an option. Place about 8 to 10 lights, clustered low on the near band (yb - (yb - yt) * (0.08 to 0.3)) rather than spread up the hillside. Give about half of them short columns, and use dayHouses at the same points for Day, all in one s-vlight isl-vwin isl-vlast path. Render Dusk and Night at 1920 and 1440 before showing him.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The four Day yachts have no reflection or wake, and DESIGN 19.3 gives every hull and sail its reflection. Mirroring about by (the hull's bottom) is geometrically right, and it stays inside the isl-ydet group. The gain is small because the yachts are only 9 to 24 px long. Keep the wake short and the reflection faint, so neither reads as clutter.

Plain in every lit version. At Dawn (whole) and Dusk (3x) each white masthead light hangs in open sky to the right of its mast top (about 13 CSS px on the nearest yacht). The rig is drawn inside rotate(heel, x, wl), but lights[0] is pushed at unrotated points. The rot() formula matches SVG's rotate(a, cx, cy), and halos follow automatically at line 726. This is exactly the 'parts do not line up' fault the owner catches first. Dropping green is right for a side-on boat heading left (port side toward the viewer). Tell him, since it removes a colour. Strictly, a white masthead light is a power vessel's steaming light; a yacht under sail shows sidelights only, or a masthead tricolour that shows red from this side. That is optional, but worth mentioning if he asks why the green went.

Confirmed in the Dawn render: a warm gold column runs down the water at x about 0.39 under an empty pink sky. Line 676 classes it 's-vglow isl-aglow'. Night hides isl-aglow (css 77) and Day hides s-vglow (css 155), but nothing hides it at Dawn. The glow above it (glowSky/glowSea) is isl-d, which Dawn hides (css 118), and Curtain Bluff's afterglow reflection is isl-d too. Adding isl-d is a one-word fix that brings Sailing Week into line with the other pieces and the sky logic.

Confirmed. The arcs sit detached ahead of the bows and read as small gulls by Day (3x right half, and every whole render). The geometry checks: at -6 degrees the rotated stem runs from (x-0.508L, wl-0.047L) to (x-0.418L, wl+0.044L), crossing wl at x-0.46L, while the spray starts at x-0.55L. The proposed aft foam line would be invisible, though. The sprays are drawn before the fleet (lines 721 to 722), and at wl+0.5 from x-0.46L to x-0.25L it lies inside the rotated hull (whose bottom there is at wl+0.026L to 0.044L), so the hull covers it.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Replace only the bow subpath with M(x-0.46L, wl) q(-0.05L, -0.9hh) (-0.15L, -0.1hh), so the wave climbs from the stem. Add the aft foam line only if sailing-week-4 lands, since only a hull seated at the waterline leaves room below it. Leave the stern wake subpaths as they are.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real. With the in-plane rotation the stern's underside rises 0.38L x sin(heel) (about 3 CSS px on the nearest yacht), and a wedge of water opens between the stern and its mirrored reflection, with the wake lines drawn in it. It is subtle at 1x, but it is the gap-where-the-sea-shows kind of fault. The clip approach works: clipPathUnits default to the user space of the referencing element, so inside the mirror the clip flips and keeps the reflection below wl, and the isl-prefixed ids are renamed by own(). At -8 degrees, though, the seated hull becomes a wedge (freeboard about 0.03L at the bow, 0.17L at the stern), which may read as nosediving. This is medium effort on an approved piece.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Seat the hull as proposed (deeper hull, clipped at wl outside the rotation, rig rotated as now). Then look at the -8 degree yacht at 1920. If the bow reads as sinking, rotate the hull by half the heel while the rig keeps the full heel. The mast foot is only 0.08L from the pivot, so it stays on the deck. Show it as a before and after, and let him choose.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed, and plainer than claimed. At Dusk (1920 3x, and at 1440) the coast rim is a warm wire across dark land, because the near hills' crest lies in front of the higher far range at every x. Its mirror crosses the water as a faint diagonal line, and Montserrat's mirrored rim shows too. s-rim is hidden only at Night (css 77), so the pale line shows at Dawn and Day as well (visible along the green hills in the Day 3x). Moving it to the far range's skyline, range.slice(1, 9), and keeping rims out of mirrored(), fixes all four versions. The hills' shapes do not change.

The boom is a good small addition. The mainsail's foot floats 0.4hh above the deck with nothing holding it, the owner's Galleon Beach photograph shows booms clearly, and a 39 px spar on the nearest yacht will read. The backstay should go. From the masthead (mx, top) to the stern (x+0.5L, wl-hh) it runs just 0.02L outside the mainsail's curved leech at mid-height. Near the foot it crosses into the sail, since the clew reaches mx+0.46L while the stay is at about mx+0.41L. Drawn after the main, it would read as a doubled leech or a stray line across the sail.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Add only the boom inside the rotated group, after the main: <path class="isl-vmast" d="M mx (wl-1.4hh) H (mx+0.48L)" stroke-width=max(0.8, L*0.014)>. It sits in `one`, so the reflection gets it too. Leave out the backstay.

missed.title: Day houses stand on the pale far range
missed.versions: Day (the same points are the coast's lights at Dawn, Sunset and Dusk)
missed.observed: By Day, two crisp white houses with red roofs (1920 whole, about x 0.63 and 0.66, y 0.535 to 0.55; also at 1440 near x 0.64) stand on the grey-blue far range (f-isl), above the green near hills' crest. They are as large and bright as the near houses, so they pop forward from the hazy distant layer, like houses floating on the haze.
missed.proposal: Keep every coast light, and so every Day house, on the near hills: clamp each light's y below the near hills' crest at its x. Lights at night stay houses by Day, and no random draw moves.

Line 687 draws y in Y(0.54 to 0.595) for x from 0.62, but the near hills' crest is at 0.58 at x 0.62 and 0.52 at x 0.7. So a light at x below about 0.68 often lands above it, on the far range.

The two r() calls keep their order (x before y, as in the original array literal), so the columns at line 691 and everything drawn after are unchanged.

missed.title: The lookout lantern's post is land-green by Day
missed.observed: By Day the lantern on the lookout's crest is an olive-green stick with a dark slate ball, standing against the turquoise bay. The post has the land's colour, not iron's.

missed.why: Line 561 draws the post with class "f-near". Every other lamp post in island-vignettes.js (lines 854, 997, 1096, 1264, 1445, 2187 and others) uses isl-vpost, which layout-art.css makes land-coloured at night (line 839) and dark iron by Day (line 245). A consistency fix of one class name.
missed.code: heights(), line 561: class="f-near" becomes class="isl-vpost". Nothing else changes, and the night versions are pixel-identical. It fits naturally alongside shirley-heights-3, which regroups the lamp.

proposals.title: Boiling-house arches break through the broken wall top
proposals.versions: all five, at 1920 and 1440 (worst at 1440, where the ruin looks like a row of little peaked huts)
proposals.observed: The ruin's path uses fill-rule evenodd. The crowns of the second and third arches sit above the lowest point of the random broken top, so the part of each arch above the wall line fills as stone. Above each opening a small stone dome sits on the wall, and a flat-topped gap cuts into the wall where the real arch head should be. At 1920 the crown is at Y(0.643) and the broken top runs from Y(0.644) to Y(0.674), so every arch clear of the gable breaks through. Only the first arch, under the gable, reads as a true arch.
proposals.proposal: Keep a band of stone over every arch. Raise the broken top by about Y(0.034) and make the arches slightly lower and narrower, so each crown sits about 3px under the lowest point the top can reach. The ruin then reads as a wall with three arched openings, with the fields seen through them.
proposals.why: A drawing that contradicts itself (the owner catches parts that do not line up). The domes are an artefact of the fill rule, not part of any ruin, and they are what makes the boiling house hard to read.
proposals.code: bettysHope(), line 1048: change `bTop + Y(0.004) + r() * Y(0.03)` to `bTop - Y(0.03) + r() * Y(0.03)`. It is still one r() call per point, so nothing else in the picture moves. Lines 1051-1052: `ar = bwid * 0.065`, and the spring `bBase - Y(0.04)` in both V commands in place of `bBase - Y(0.05)`. Check: crown at 1920 is about Y(0.661) against a top of at most Y(0.64); at 1440 it is about 3px clear. Side benefit: the course loop at line 1056 (`y > bTop`) draws its top line at Y(0.648), which today can float above the broken top; it now falls inside the wall.
proposals.truth_to_place: Real place, but there is no photograph in the folder. This is an internal correction: the arches stay, and nothing the ruin lacks is added.

proposals.title: The mill cap turns the corner with the tower
proposals.observed: The restored tower's right side is in shade from mx+Y(0.025) outward, but the wooden cap and its roof above it are one flat brown with no shade. This is the Court House problem again: the shaded face stops where the cap begins. The cap overhangs the tower but casts no shadow on it.
proposals.proposal: Carry the tower's shade line straight up through the cap body and the right-hand part of its roof, as the Court House side shade now carries through the cornice, parapet and coping. Add a thin shadow under the cap's overhang across the top of the tower (about 2px), as the Court House cornice casts.
proposals.why: In the owner's words from today, a drawing that shows two faces of a form keeps to them all the way up. The cap is where the eye goes (the sails hang from it), so a continuous shade line from the tower's foot to the cap's roof makes the mill read as one solid, turned form.
proposals.code: bettysHope(). After line 1085 (the tower shade), add the cap's cast shadow: `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="M${F(mx - mwt / 2)} ${F(capY + 1)}h${F(mwt)}v${F(Y(0.016))}h${F(-mwt)}Z"/>`. After line 1088, add the cap's shaded side, both subpaths wound the same way: `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="M${F(mx + Y(0.025))} ${F(capY + 1)}V${F(capY - capH)}H${F(mx + capW / 2)}V${F(capY + 1)}ZM${F(mx + Y(0.025))} ${F(capY - capH + 1)}V${F(capY - capH - Y(0.035))}H${F(mx + capW * 0.3)}L${F(mx + capW / 2 + Y(0.01))} ${F(capY - capH + 1)}Z"/>`. The sails are drawn afterwards, so they stay on top.
proposals.truth_to_place: Real place, but there is no photograph in the folder. This is form consistency only: it shades the cap the drawing already has and adds no feature.

proposals.title: Complete the mill lamp: a pool on the ground and a cap
proposals.versions: pool at Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night (with the other lights); cap in all five
proposals.observed: The lamp by the mill door lights last (isl-vlast) and has a halo, but it lays no pool of its own. Only the edge of the door's pool reaches its foot. The lamp itself is a bare rectangle on a post. Every other lamp on the site (Court House lanterns, the fort lamp, the step lanterns) has a pyramid cap, so by Day this one reads as a stump.
proposals.proposal: Give the lamp its own small pool of light on the ground in the vlast group, so its arrival at the end of the pass shows on the ground. Add a small pyramid cap over the lamp in isl-vpost, like the fort lamp's.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.4: every light is a set (light, halo, pool). The last light is the focal one, and today its arrival adds only a halo. The cap makes it read as a lantern at a glance in every version.
proposals.code: bettysHope(). Before line 1096 (the post), add `<g class="isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:4">${pool(lx, mb + Y(0.015), Y(0.1), Y(0.03), 0.6)}</g>`. After line 1097, add `<path class="isl-vpost" d="M${F(lx - Y(0.018))} ${F(mb - Y(0.175))}L${F(lx)} ${F(mb - Y(0.197))}L${F(lx + Y(0.018))} ${F(mb - Y(0.175))}Z"/>` (about 5 by 3 CSS px at 1920).
proposals.truth_to_place: Not a feature of the landmark: an estate lamp the drawing already has, completed to the site's lamp standard.

proposals.title: Estate house: shadow under the eaves, pool at the lit door
proposals.versions: eave shadow in all five; door pool at Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night
proposals.observed: The hipped roof overhangs the wall by Y(0.02) on each side, but the wall under it is evenly lit to the eave line, so the roof looks pasted on. The lit door has no light on the ground; only the broad halo reaches it. The mill door, by contrast, has a pool.
proposals.proposal: Add a thin band of shade (about 2px) along the wall's top under the eaves, as the Court House cornice casts. Add a small pool of warm light on the ground at the foot of the lit door, in the same group as the windows.
proposals.why: The shadow under an overhang is what shows the roof projecting. The door pool makes the house's light a set, consistent with the mill door beside it.
proposals.code: bettysHope(). After line 1036: `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="M${F(hx0)} ${F(hTop + 1)}H${F(hx0 + hw)}v${F(Y(0.016))}H${F(hx0)}Z"/>` (the windows start at hTop+Y(0.035), so they are clear). After line 1043: `<g class="isl-vwin" style="--i:1">${pool(hx0 + hw * 0.5, hBot + Y(0.02), Y(0.13), Y(0.035), 0.6)}</g>` (the door is the i=2 opening, centred at hx0+hw*0.5).
proposals.truth_to_place: Real estate, but there is no photograph in the folder. Both are light and shade on forms already drawn.

proposals.title: Twin tower's shade stops short of its broken crown
proposals.observed: The shaded face of the roofless twin is a polygon whose top is the flat line twin.top. The broken crown rises up to Y(0.008) above that line between X(0.5)+Y(0.028) and X(0.5)+Y(0.09), so a thin lit sliver of stone sits on top of the shaded face. At 3x it shows as a pale lip at the top right of the tower. It is the same kind of shade that stops short of the top as today's Court House fix, though small (about 1.2 CSS px at its highest).
proposals.proposal: Run the shade polygon's top along the broken crown on the shaded side, so the shade reaches the top of the stone.
proposals.why: The shaded face should reach the top of the form. It is a small change, and it keeps the corner rule consistent across the two mills.
proposals.code: bettysHope(), line 1073. Replace `L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.02))} ${F(twin.top)}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.09))} ${F(twin.top)}` with `L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.02))} ${F(twin.top + Y(0.003))}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.054))} ${F(twin.top - Y(0.008))}L${F(X(0.5) + Y(0.09))} ${F(twin.top)}`. These points follow tower()'s broken branch (line 1062): crown points at cx+wt*0.05 (top+Y(0.006)), cx+wt*0.3 (top-Y(0.008)) and cx+wt/2 (top), with wt = Y(0.18).
proposals.truth_to_place: Real place, but there is no photograph in the folder. This is form consistency only.

proposals.title: Tail-pole wheel tangled in the drying racks
proposals.observed: The cart wheel at the tail pole's foot is centred at mx+capW*0.3+Y(0.26) (about mx+Y(0.33), radius Y(0.028)). The first two racks start at mx+mwb/2+Y(0.08) and step by Y(0.1), so the wheel sits on top of the second rack (it spans Y(0.32) to Y(0.405)) and touches the first. The wheel, pole foot and rails read as one tangle of brown lines.
proposals.proposal: Start the racks just beyond the wheel so the tail pole's foot and its wheel stand clear on the ground, with the three racks in a row after it.
proposals.why: Parts that overlap without meaning read as a drawing error. The tail wheel is the detail that explains how the cap turns, so it should read on its own.
proposals.code: bettysHope(), line 1101: `rx0 = mx + capW * 0.3 + Y(0.26) + Y(0.05) + i * Y(0.1)`. The last rack ends near X(0.86) at 1920 and X(0.87) at 1440, clear of the palm at X(0.95).
proposals.truth_to_place: Real place, but there is no photograph in the folder. Only existing elements are rearranged.

proposals.title: String course crosses the shaded side face lit
proposals.versions: all five (clearest by Day and at Sunset)
proposals.observed: The string course between the floors (an isl-vstone band from x0-Y(0.006) to x1+sd+Y(0.006), line 1191) is drawn after the side face's shade. It crosses the shaded side as a light stripe, while the cornice, parapet and coping above it now turn the corner into shade.
proposals.proposal: Turn the string course's side portion into the same shade, at its own projecting corner (x1+Y(0.006)), exactly as today's corner does for the cornice and coping.
proposals.why: This is the same corner the owner called an absolutely beautiful addition. The one course left lit breaks the effect halfway down the building.
proposals.code: courtHouse(), after line 1192, reusing turn(): `s += `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="${turn(mid - Y(0.004), mid + Y(0.016), Y(0.006))}"/>`;`. It must come after line 1191, because the turn shade at line 1184 is drawn before the band and is covered by it.

proposals.title: Quoins returning round the corner onto the side face

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the renders and the code. At 1440 Day the boiling house reads as a gabled hut plus three small domed huts. With evenodd, each arch crown sits above the random broken top: at 1920 the crown is at Y(0.6435) and the top runs Y(0.644) to Y(0.674), so the part of each arch above the wall fills as a dome. The fix is correct. It keeps one r() per point, clears each crown by about 3px at both widths (3.07 at 1920, 3.3 at 1440), and moves the top course line inside the wall. Two gaps remain. Raising the whole top by Y(0.03) cuts the gable's rise to 5 to 9px, so it reads less clearly. And from the code, the courses (line 1056) are still drawn across the three openings, over the fields.
verdicts.revised_proposal: As proposed: the top at `bTop - Y(0.03) + r() * Y(0.03)`, `ar = bwid * 0.065`, and the spring at `bBase - Y(0.04)`. Also lift the gable's peak and shoulder by the same Y(0.03) (Y(0.575) to Y(0.545), Y(0.615) to Y(0.585)) so it keeps its present rise. In the course loop, build each line as segments that skip every opening. Below the spring, skip cx +/- ar. In the arch head, skip cx +/- sqrt(ar^2 - (spring - y)^2). That way no joint crosses the field seen through an arch. Render 1440 Day, where the fault is worst, before and after.

But a vertical shade line run up through a hipped roof and along its ridge does not follow a real face (DESIGN 19.3: planes must follow the form's faces). On a hip roof the side face is the hip end, bounded by the diagonal hip line. vpshade (near at 30%) on dark wood will be subtle, and the sails cover part of the cap, so the value is modest.
