verdicts.reason: Confirmed in week-calendar_1920_sunset_whole.png: three strokes from the hub, one hour hand just left of straight down (18:30), a second at about 7:30 (19:30) and the shared minute hand. layout-art.css hides .isl-d only at Night (line 70) and at Dawn/Day (line 118), so at Sunset both isl-s and isl-d hands show; at Dusk only isl-d, which is correct. The fix is feasible either way (an isl-lq data-q="d" wrapper, lines 528-532, or the one-line CSS rule) and uses no rng. A clock showing two times is exactly the kind of slip the owner catches.

Confirmed: the crown is near-black navy at Dusk and Night (dusk right-half 3x, night right-half 3x) and navy at Dawn and Sunset. By Day it is green because only .isl[data-sky=day] .isl-shrub retints it. shrubs() returns 'f-near isl-shrub' (line 894), so the string replace works. .isl .isl-tshade maps to --isl-lshade (line 587), which has a green value in every version (lines 448, 457, 466, 475, 484). The Day rule (0,3,0) still outranks (0,2,0). The replace changes no r() calls. The plant then stays a plant in every version, as the rule that only light changes requires.

Both collisions are visible at every size. The red dot at [2,2] sits on the third X's upper-right arm, since 0.72+0.30 lies on the anti-diagonal x+y=1 (dusk left-half 3x). The blue dot at [5,3] touches the ring's lower edge (day whole, dusk right-half 3x). I checked the new cells: [5,2] sits inside the ring, clear of its top stroke. [5,4] is at about (448, 231) CSS px at 1920, about 26 px clear of the plant's crown. No rng. The event later this week inside the ring is a small addition that fits the page's title.

Confirmed. The calendar's drop shadow is a dark strip about 4 px wide down its right edge, inside the sconce's warm halo (dusk right-half 3x), and the clock's shadow falls to the lower right. Both lights (window and sconce) are to the right. A right-down drop is the house convention (tool wall 1877, committee room 2521/2548), but the committee room's window is on the left, so its shadows agree with its light and this room's do not. The flip is trivial, and the left strip is clear of the clock (its right edge is about 34 px from the calendar at 1920). The paper covers the bottom-left. Low value because it is subtle.

Confirmed. When lit, the shade is a dark bronze bucket with no glowing mouth (night and dusk right-half 3x), unlike the tool wall's bulb ellipse and the desk lamp's bulb. The cone's right edge also crosses the lower-left glass of the window (a faint diagonal haze in the dusk 3x). The Y(0.07) foot does not fully fix the haze: at 1440 (W 680, H 322) the calendar-to-window gap is only about 34 px, so half is about 17 px, and Y(0.07) = 22.5 px still reaches the glass.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Add the lit mouth exactly as proposed: <ellipse class="isl-tbulb" cx=lx cy=ly+Y(0.07) rx=Y(0.026) ry=Y(0.008)/>, inside the isl-vlamps group, which is drawn before the shade so the shade covers its upper half. Make the cone's foot follow the wall gap rather than a fixed width: const cf = Math.min(Y(0.12), (f.wx0 - (cx0 + cw)) / 2 - Y(0.012)); and use [lx + cf, Y(0.62)], [lx - cf, Y(0.62)]. The light then stays on the wall between the calendar and the window frame at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120. Check the Night and Dusk renders at each width.

verdicts.reason: Observation true: windowView's two boats have no reflections (day right-half 3x), while the far land is mirrored and toolWall line 1861 mirrors each boat. The code is feasible: extract the hull string and add the 0.15 mirrored group. It uses no rng. The wall drawn after windowView hides any mast reflection below wB, for example boat 2's reflection, which would reach 0.79H. The gain is small, since a 0.8-px mast at 0.15 opacity barely shows. Its main worth is consistency with DESIGN 19.3 across the three news windows.

Confirmed at Dusk and Night (right-half 3x). The middle boat's mast and masthead light are hidden behind the mullion at 0.5, while its forestay, its hull and a broken light column still show under the bar. A light column with no light breaks DESIGN 19.4 and is the kind of stray the owner catches. Moving the boat to fx 0.4 keeps the r() count: streakList's loop depends on y and H, not bx. At 1920 the boat at 0.4 is 41 px from the one at 0.2 (hull half-widths 7.5 and 5.9 px), and its mast top (0.352H) stays below the transom (0.318H plus 1 px).

The code confirms it: line 1869 draws the jamb strip from wx0 inward. The window sits at 573 to 777 px in an 814-px card at 1920, so the viewer at the centre is to its left and can see only the right jamb. The shared windowWall (line 2196) puts the strip on the outer jamb (side 1 gives wx1 for right-hand windows), and the four later window pieces follow it. This is the same face-consistency family as the clock tower fix. Using windowWall(W, H, toolFrame(W, H), 'isltwallg', 1) gives identical sizes (rv, frame and mullion widths match) and removes the duplicate defs. Faint at 0.18/0.1 opacity, so low value.

Plausible and consistent with the Sunset whole render: the Sun's glow sits right under the transom, which crosses the top of the disc (54.6 to 73.3 against the bar at 59.2 at 1920). But the main proposal, 18:26 at the current bearing, sinks about 30% of the disc into the far hill: at fx 0.7 the hill top is at about 75.7 px against a disc bottom of 81.3. That undoes the '18:23, disc standing on the hill' choice recorded in PIECES and DESIGN 19.6. So the optional turn has to be part of the change. At 1920 no minute clears the bar by 3 px and also stands on the hill at 0.7.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Change both together: sunset '18:26' and face at f.ww * 0.86 in place of 0.7 (line 2995). At 0.86 the hill is about 0.029H, so the disc (62.6 to 81.3 at 1920, 58.5 to 74.1 at 1440) clears the transom's lower edge by about 2.4 px at 1920 and 3.8 px at 1440, and stands on the hill with about 1 px hidden. It stays about 26 px from the right frame, and its path runs just right of the boat at 0.78. The Moon and Venus are unaffected, since they are placed by moonAt. Update the PIECES comment. Re-render Sunset and Dusk (the glow moves with the bearing) at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120. If 2.4 px reads as touching, use 18:27 at the same face.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed (day left-half 3x): one hook above each middle driver and middle chisel, the outer tools hanging from nothing, and the tape hanging by a clip with no peg about 6 px below the chisel tip. A rack under the ferrules is how screwdrivers really hang. At 1920 it is about 29 by 3 px in isl-lwood, readable without clutter. The offsets check out: the drivers span ±0.13ts, so a ±0.14 rack at 0.225 covers them; the chisels span ±0.116, so ±0.125 at 0.168 does. Add the rack to `board` after the tool group so it sits in front. The tape peg (0.39 to 0.44ts) is only about 0.5 px clear of the chisel outline, so shorten it to start at 0.395. A true small detail, modest gain.

Confirmed at Day and Dusk (left-half 3x): the bench hammer reads as a boot. A flat handle runs into the foot of an upright head, and the claw flares away from the handle. Drawing it from TOOLS.hammer(u) (u = ts, the same scale as the outline above) makes the match with the empty outline immediate. But at 76 degrees the handle's lower corner (0.028, 0.58) lands at y' 0.1675u, about 0.024u (2.5 px at 1920) below the claw tip's 0.143u, so the butt sinks into the bench. The proposal does ask for tuning.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Use rotate(78.7): tan = 0.51/0.102 = 5 puts the claw tip (0.13, 0.07) and the handle's butt corner (0.028, 0.58) at the same height, 0.141u. So: const hm = TOOLS.hammer(u); hammerFlat = `<g transform="translate(${F(hammerX + u * 0.32)} ${F(tTop - u * 0.141)}) rotate(78.7)">${hm.parts.map(([c, d]) => `<path class="${c}" d="${d}"/>`).join('')}</g>`. The hammer then rests on its claw tip and butt, face up, the handle sloping about 11 degrees. It spans about hammerX-0.24u to +0.30u, clear of the vise and the pencil. Delete hx. It stays in the isl-lq 'aysd' group.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at Night (whole and right-half 3x): a bright dot at the window's top-left inner corner, half under the frame, reads as a screw head or stray highlight. At Dusk (y about 15.5) only the halo glows at the corner. L.planets(v, m, boxes, cls) already skips any planet within 11 px of a box (island-core.js 236 and 474), so passing the bars from a PIECES hook through build() line 3345 works. The Moon is unaffected. It also covers the prompt desk's Venus against its top bar (visible in prompt-desk_1920_dusk_left-half_3x). Medium effort, and Venus will usually drop from this short pane, but a clean removal beats a half-hidden dot. Date-dependent, so test with ?isl-moon=.

The strongest Sun issue in the set. In prompt-desk_1920_dawn_whole.png the transom runs straight through the middle of the rising Sun (centre 76.2, bar 75.3 at 1920). Raising the transom is the right move, but 0.28 with the Moon at 0.2 leaves the Moon (r 13.1) filling a 30.5-px pane with about 2 px margins, which looks jammed. Check the numbers: at 0.30, the bar is at 0.25H = 60.75 (bottom edge 62.1), the Sun's top (65.7) clears it by 3.6 px, and the upper pane (26.5 to 59.4, 32.9 px) holds the Moon with about 3.4 px each side. At 1440 (W 680, H 221) the Sun clears by 6.8 px and the Moon (r 10.9) has 4 px margins.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Set the transom at 0.30 of the window's height (line 1993: (wB - wT) * 0.42 -> * 0.30), a top light over taller lower panes. Centre the Moon's place in the new upper pane: moonAt y = (f.wT + (f.hz - f.wT) * 0.22) / H (line 3010). At 1920 the Sun is then whole in the lower pane about 3.6 px under the bar, and Venus moves behind the wall above the window, with any glow at the frame removed by tool-wall-6's keep-out. Re-render Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night at 1920, 1440, 1280 and 1120. If 1280 or 1120 come out tighter, use the adaptive form: transom y = min(0.42 frac, hz - SKY.a.sun[1]*ppd - 1.12*sunR(W) - 4), with the Moon centred in whatever upper pane results.

verdicts.reason: Code confirmed: line 1991 draws the jamb strip at wx1, and the render shows it on the right inside edge (day left-half 3x, x about 738 to 750). The window spans about 33 to 252 px of 814, so the viewer is to its right and only the left jamb faces them. windowWall(..., -1) (the committee room's left window) draws it on the left. Same fix family as the clock tower and the mill doors, and it agrees with the later windows. Faint, so low value.

Confirmed at Dusk (left-half 3x): the sail's masthead light is lit with nothing on the water beneath, while the cay's light beside it has its broken column and the cay is mirrored. The bright white sail has no reflection. The code is feasible, and using a fresh rng(617) is correct: r feeds the handwriting lengths, the book offsets and the sparks, which would all shift otherwise. s-vglow is hidden by Day (css line 155). The mirrored sail reaches about 0.578H, inside the window (wB 0.6H). This completes the light set (DESIGN 19.4) on the window's brightest object.

Confirmed (day right-half 3x): the pen is a slanted stick rising from the desk's back edge into the wall, floating. The proposed path correctly keeps it inside the top band (dTop+0.006 to dTop+0.031) and clear of the stand's lip (which ends at nx+0.58nW). But the pen is isl-lbk1, which on the desk top is almost the desk's own colour: Day #9c4b40 on #9b4a2c, Dusk #7d3b35 on #7a3a24, Night #4d2522 on #5a2618. Moved onto the wood unchanged, it would vanish.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Use the proposed in-band path and recolour the pen so it reads on the wood: class isl-lbk2 (the notebook-cover blue, #3f6b92 by Day) or isl-tiron (near-black). Optionally add a 1-px isl-lalu clip near its far end. Check Day and Night at 1920 and 1440, where the band is 8.5 and 7.7 px deep.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed: by Day the mug (#f6f3ee) nearly disappears on the cream wall (#f1ece2) in the prompt desk (day right-half 3x) and on the calendar page in the week calendar (day whole). The eye is above the mug (hz 0.45H, mug top about 0.63H, and about 0.71H on the shelf), so showing its opening is correct perspective. A dark coffee oval makes it a mug at a glance. The shade sides are right: away from the left window here, away from the right window and sconce in the calendar. One small tweak: start the side shade at mt + Y(0.008), below the rim, so it does not dim the coffee oval. The library's flat-topped mugs (line 1665) could follow later for consistency.

Observation true: the orb's halo (3 × orr) has faded to about 0.03 by the desk top 78 px below, and nothing under the orb is lit (night whole). A pool completes the light set. But by Day a teal pool at about 31% alpha over the red-brown wood mixes to a dull grey-brown smear. Also, an ellipse given the isl-vglow class directly would have its .7 opacity overridden to 1 by the isl-vlight animation, which uses fill-mode both. The existing lamps avoid this by putting the pool inside an isl-vlamps group.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Lay the pool only in the lit versions. Put it in its own group, <g class="isl-vlamps isl-vwin isl-vlast" style="--i:3">, just before the orb's group: <ellipse cx=ox cy=dTop+Y(0.014) rx=orr*1.6 ry=Y(0.016) fill="url(#islporbh)" opacity=".55"/>. It then comes on with the orb, stays under the orb's own drawing and is absent by Day (css line 155), matching the tool wall's lamp group. It reaches only 0.5 px up the mug's base. Check Night and Dusk for colour on the wood.

missed.title: The mug keeps its evening white at Night
missed.versions: Night and the dark scheme (week calendar and prompt desk)
missed.observed: At Night every material darkens: the calendar page and the folded paper go to --isl-lpage #a79f8c. The mug stays #e6e2da, its Dusk value, so it is the brightest unlit thing in the dark room and reads as lit, brighter than the paper right beside it. The prompt desk shows the same at Night (prompt-desk_1920_night_right-half_3x: the mug outshines the books' page edges). layout-art.css sets --isl-lmug only at line 534 (the default) and line 538 (Day); the Night/slate block has no value for it.
missed.proposal: Give the mug a Night value, stepped down as the paper is (#e8e0cc to #a79f8c is about ×0.71): --isl-lmug: #a7a399. The mug, the calendar and the paper then take the same light, and the mug stays the pale thing it is.
missed.why: Objects are identical in every version and only the light changes, but this one object ignores the Night light and looks switched on. It is the one thing in both rooms that does not darken.
missed.code: layout-art.css after line 540: [data-md-color-scheme="slate"] .isl:where(:not([data-sky])), .isl[data-sky="night"] { --isl-lmug: #a7a399; }. The .isl-lmug and .isl-lmugh rules (548-549) pick it up for the body and the handle. The library's mugs sit in isl-lq groups that are hidden at Night, so only these two pieces change.

missed.title: The vise reads as a small window
missed.observed: At the bench's left end, the vise is two dark jaw blocks with light top edges, a light horizontal bar across both of them at mid-height (the screw, drawn over the jaws), and a light vertical bar at the left (the hanging handle). At the picture's size the light cross over two dark squares reads as a little four-paned window or a grille, not a vise. The same reading shows in tool-wall_1440_day_whole.png and the Night renders.
missed.proposal: Draw the screw behind the jaws, as a real screw passes through them. It then shows only in the gap between the jaws and between the outer jaw and the handle. Keep the hanging handle bar in front. The light cross goes, and the two jaws read as clamped on a screw with its bar hanging at the end.
missed.why: The owner's caution is that a detail which does not read when stylised is fixed or left out, and he prefers fixing. A vise is a strong 'workshop' cue on the Tool Directory's picture, and at present it reads as a stray small window at the card's edge.
missed.code: toolWall lines 1918-1920: split the isl-lalu path. Emit `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(vx + u * 0.005, vT + jh * 0.45, u * 0.26, u * 0.018)}"/>` (the screw) BEFORE the isl-tiron jaws/base path. Then the jaws, the isl-tjaw strokes, and last `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(vx - u * 0.005, vT + jh * 0.05, u * 0.016, jh * 0.95)}"/>` (the handle). No rng, nothing else moves. Look at it at 1920 and 1440 in Day and Night before showing it.

proposals.title: Stand the bed and drip stand on the floor
proposals.observed: The bed's wheels stop at Y(0.86) and the floor line (where the wall meets the floor) is at fl = Y(0.9). So the whole bed hangs about 9 CSS px above the floor at 1920, against the wall. The drip stand's base bar is at fl - Y(0.02), about 4 px above the floor line. The chair's legs end exactly on the line. Nothing has a contact shadow. In the day 3x left half, the wheel's bottom is at y=585 and the floor line at 610.
proposals.proposal: Bring every floor contact down into the floor band, in front of the wall. Lower the wheels so their feet sit at about Y(0.93). Put the drip stand's foot at fl + Y(0.025). Take the chair legs to fl + Y(0.012). Lay a soft isl-tdrop ellipse under each one, as the committee room does under its chairs and table.
proposals.why: Right now the bed reads as floating or hung on the wall. The owner rejects floating objects. It also brings the bed closer to real hospital-bed proportions (mattress top at about 0.29 of its length above the floor, up from 0.15).
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2320: bLeg = Y(0.8) -> Y(0.87). The wheels at line 2323 follow (cy = bLeg + Y(0.03), foot at Y(0.93)). Right after line 2321 add s += `<ellipse class="isl-tdrop" cx="${F((b0 + b1) / 2)}" cy="${F(Y(0.93))}" rx="${F((b1 - b0) / 2 + Y(0.02))}" ry="${F(Y(0.012))}"/>`. Line 2332: both `fl - Y(0.02)` -> `fl + Y(0.025)` (the pole's foot and the base bar), with an ellipse under the bar (cx ix, cy fl + Y(0.025), rx Y(0.08), ry Y(0.008)) drawn before the pole. Line 2353: chair legs `V${F(fl)}` -> `V${F(fl + Y(0.012))}`, plus an ellipse at (chx, fl + Y(0.012), Y(0.09), Y(0.008)) drawn before the chair.

proposals.title: Hang the drip bag from its hook, with a drip chamber
proposals.observed: The stand's hook bar is at iT + Y(0.01) and the bag's top at bagT = iT + Y(0.03). Nothing joins them, so the bag floats about 4.5 CSS px below the bar (y=88 vs 100 in the 3x half). The line leaves straight from the bag's bottom.
proposals.proposal: Add a short hanger from the bar's right end down to the bag's top centre (both are at ix + Y(0.05)). Add the small clear drip chamber under the bag, and start the line from the bottom of that chamber.
proposals.why: Right now the bag floats, which is exactly what the owner catches. The drip chamber is the detail that makes it read as an IV set rather than a pouch on a pole, which suits the Clinical Practice title.
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), lines 2332-2336. After the pole add `<path class="isl-hframe" d="M${F(ix + Y(0.05))} ${F(iT + Y(0.01))}V${F(bagT + Y(0.004))}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(0.8, Y(0.007)))}"/>`. After the fluid add `<path class="isl-hbag" d="${rect(ix + Y(0.043), bagB - Y(0.006), Y(0.014), Y(0.036))}"/>` (3 by 8 CSS px at 1920). In the isl-hcord line, change the start `M${F(ix + Y(0.05))} ${F(bagB)}` to `...${F(bagB + Y(0.03))}`.

proposals.title: A wall plate for the monitor's arm
proposals.observed: The monitor's 'wall arm' is a rounded stub from mx0 - Y(0.05) to mx0 at mid-height. It ends in mid-air on the wall with nothing holding it (x 516 to 556, y 162 in the day 3x half).
proposals.proposal: Add a small upright mounting plate at the arm's left end, about Y(0.018) wide and Y(0.07) tall, in the arm's metal. Optionally add a thin isl-tdrop shadow of the monitor on the wall (offset Y(0.01), Y(0.013), as the calendar and whiteboard have).
proposals.why: An arm that stops in the air reads as floating. The plate says 'fixed to the wall', like the brackets under the week-calendar shelf. The shadow separates the dark monitor from the wall at Dusk and Night.
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2340: after the isl-hframe arm add `<path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(mx0 - Y(0.066), mT + mh * 0.5 - Y(0.035), Y(0.018), Y(0.07))}"/>`. Optionally, before the isl-tiron monitor rect on line 2341, add `<path class="isl-tdrop" d="${rect(mx0 + Y(0.01), mT + Y(0.013), mw, mh)}"/>`.

proposals.title: Columns on the water under the window's hill lights
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (s-vglow is hidden by Day). windowView is shared, so it also fixes committee-room and week-calendar
proposals.observed: windowView's comment promises 'a few lights on them with their columns on the water'. The code draws the six hill lights (line 2211) but gives a streakList column only to each boat's masthead (line 2218). In the night renders the lights sit on the hills with nothing on the water below (3x right half: 641,288; 789,285; 931,302; 1067,283).
proposals.proposal: Give each hill light a short, faint broken column on the water. Use a narrower spread and lower opacity than the boats' columns, so the six stay quiet in a small window.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.4: 'Every light is a set: the light itself, its halo, and its column on the water'. The task list also names 'a light over water with no column' as a correction.
proposals.code: windowView(), after line 2211 and before the boats loop: `const rl = rng(4057); for (const [lx] of lights) s += dashes(streakList(lx, y0 + 1, H, rl, 0.03, 0.025), 's-vglow', 1, [0.05, 0.1, 0.18]);`. Its own rng stream keeps the boats' streaks, and the week-calendar's shrubs drawn later from r, unchanged. The wall drawn after covers everything outside the window.

proposals.title: The reading lamp's light landing on the bed
proposals.versions: Dawn, Sunset, Dusk, Night (inside the lamp's isl-vlamps group, so off by Day)
proposals.observed: The lamp has its halo and a cone (islvspill) that fades out just above the blanket at bTop - Y(0.04). Nothing shows where the light lands, so the cone stops in the air.
proposals.proposal: Add a soft warm pool on the blanket's upper side under the lamp, centred where the cone meets the bed.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3/19.4: a pool under every lamp completes the set (the committee room pools its lamp on the table). A warm patch on the blue blanket also draws the eye to the bed, the subject.
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2349: inside the isl-vlamps group, after the spill path, append `${pool(lx, bTop - Y(0.01), Y(0.19), Y(0.04), 0.45)}`.

proposals.title: The mesh band at the top of the privacy curtain
proposals.observed: The cubicle curtain is solid fabric from its track down to its hem.
proposals.proposal: Make the curtain's top band, from Y(0.045) to about Y(0.13), an open mesh. Lay the wall gradient over it at about 0.55 opacity so the wall shows through, with a fine grid of isl-hfold lines and a seam line at its foot. The folds continue below.
proposals.why: Hospital cubicle curtains really do have this open mesh top (it lets sprinklers and air through). It is the detail that separates a hospital curtain from a home one, which strengthens the Clinical Practice link at a glance. At about 23 CSS px tall it reads as a pale band even where single threads do not.
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), after line 2318: `const mB = Y(0.13); let mesh = ''; for (let x = X(0.005); x < cx1; x += Y(0.018)) mesh += `M${F(x)} ${F(Y(0.045))}V${F(mB)}`; for (let y = Y(0.06); y < mB; y += Y(0.018)) mesh += `M-2 ${F(y)}H${F(cx1 + Y(0.004))}`; s += `<path fill="url(#islhwallg)" opacity=".55" d="${rect(-2, Y(0.045), cx1 + 2 + Y(0.004), mB - Y(0.045))}"/><path class="isl-hfold" d="${mesh}" stroke-width=".6"/><path class="isl-hfold" d="M-2 ${F(mB)}H${F(cx1 + Y(0.004))}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1, Y(0.01)))}"/>`;` (islhwallg is already defined by windowWall).

proposals.title: Keep the chair clear of the bed's foot at narrow widths
proposals.versions: all five, at narrower windows (computed, not seen)
proposals.observed: The chair's left edge is at wx0 - Y(0.2) = 0.695W - 0.2H (while ww is clamped at 0.26W), and the bed's foot is at b1 = 0.62W. The gap is 0.075W - 0.2H: about 16 CSS px at 1920 and 10 px at 1440, as rendered. It reaches zero when W/H is about 2.67, which could happen at 1120 to 1280 when the card grows taller. The chair's seat would then overlap the bed's foot post.
proposals.proposal: Clamp the chair's place so it never comes nearer the bed than a small margin.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.5 asks for checks at 1280 and 1120, because things placed from the width and things sized from the height meet there and nowhere else.
proposals.code: hospitalRoom(), line 2351: `const chx = Math.max(f.wx0 - Y(0.12), b1 + Y(0.12));`. Check with art_review.py at 1280 and 1120 before and after.

proposals.title: The third high window runs under the screen
proposals.versions: all five, at every width (worse at 1440)
proposals.observed: The windows are at X(0.12), X(0.32) and X(0.52), each Y(0.36) wide. The screen's frame starts at X(0.62) - Y(0.012). So the third window's right frame and most of its third pane disappear behind the screen at 1920 (window 843-1005, screen from 1003 in the 2x image). At 1440 half the third pane is gone. The two meet whenever W/H < 3.72, which covers every card shown.
proposals.proposal: Space the three windows evenly between X(0.12) and a margin left of the screen, so the third window ends about Y(0.07) short of the frame. Move the Moon's baked place with the middle window.
proposals.why: A window cut off by the screen reads as a collision, and the three windows lose their rhythm. The owner catches both (misaligned parts, windows out of rhythm).
proposals.code: lectureHall(), line 2366: `const ww = Y(0.36), wT = Y(0.08), wB = Y(0.3), wL = X(0.12), wR = X(0.62) - Y(0.07) - ww, wins = [wL, (wL + wR) / 2, wR];`. At 1920 this gives gaps of about 72 CSS px, at 1440 about 51, and at W/H near 2.7 still about 26. PIECES['lecture-hall'].moonAt (line 3060), the middle window's centre: `(W, H) => [(W * 0.37 - H * 0.035) / W, 0.15]`.

proposals.title: The front wall shows through the seats to the picture's foot
proposals.observed: The seat backs are separate paths with gaps (step 1.15 x size) and nothing behind them. So the pale front-wall gradient shows between the seats below floor level. Where the two rows' gaps coincide (x about 245, 720 and 1195 in the 2x image; 368 and 1080 in the day 3x left half), a wall-coloured strip runs from the rail straight to the bottom edge.
proposals.proposal: Before the rows, lay a band of floor in shade (isl-lfloor under an isl-tdrop) from just under the front rail, Y(0.78), to the bottom. The gaps then show the shadowed tiers instead of the lit wall. It also hides the lectern and the skeleton's pole below the rail, so both stand behind it as on a stage.
proposals.why: This is the same kind of flaw as the cruise ship's sliver: the background showing through where solid form should be. The occlusion also grounds the lectern (DESIGN 19.3, 'a low wall in front of a tripod's feet').
proposals.code: lectureHall(), before the loop at line 2408: `const tier = rect(-2, Y(0.78), W + 4, H - Y(0.78) + 2); s += `<path class="isl-lfloor" d="${tier}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${tier}"/>`;`.

proposals.title: Collarbones to join the skeleton's arms to its body
proposals.observed: Each arm starts at (kx ± 1.1u, top + 1.7u), about 0.25u outside the end of the top rib. Nothing joins it to the spine (there are no clavicles), so the arms hang beside the rib cage unattached. There are also no hands or feet: the limbs end in bare sticks at the wrists and ankles.
proposals.proposal: Draw the two clavicles, slightly S-curved, from the top of the sternum (kx, top + 1.55u) out to each shoulder point where the humerus starts. Optionally add small hands (short strokes below each wrist) and feet (short strokes turned out at each ankle).
proposals.why: On the Medical Education page, a skeleton whose arms are not attached is the kind of anatomical slip a medical educator notices. The clavicles make the shoulder girdle read at a glance. At u of about 11 CSS px they are 2.3 px strokes, 12 px long, so they read.

proposals.title: The projector the beam comes from
proposals.versions: all five (the body in every version; the beam as now)
proposals.observed: The beam (islvspill, 0.5 opacity) starts from a point at the picture's top edge, X(0.8), y = -2. With no projector there, the part above the screen shows at Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night as a pale, unexplained wedge in the top-right corner (1050-1340, y 0-30 in the 2x images). Its right edge also runs to the screen's bottom-right corner instead of its top-right, so the triangle above the screen is lopsided.
proposals.proposal: Hang a small ceiling projector at the apex: a short drop rod from the top edge and a dark box, seen from behind, from about Y(0.012) to Y(0.04). Start the beam from its lower middle, and make the beam's outline the true hull of lens and screen: lens, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, top-left.
proposals.why: Keeps and fixes a feature (the docstring's 'projector's light', always on) rather than removing it. A pale shape with no source reads as a stray patch; with the projector it reads as light.
proposals.code: lectureHall(), line 2379 becomes `const pjx = X(0.8), pjy = Y(0.035); s += `<path d="${polyD([[pjx - Y(0.015), pjy], [pjx + Y(0.015), pjy], [sx1, sT], [sx1, sB], [sx0, sB], [sx0, sT]])}" fill="url(#islvspill)" opacity=".5"/>`;`. After line 2380 add `s += `<path class="isl-tiron" d="${rect(pjx - 1, -2, 2, Y(0.014) + 2)}${rect(pjx - Y(0.055), Y(0.012), Y(0.11), Y(0.028))}"/>`;`. The body ends at Y(0.04), clear of the screen frame at Y(0.068).

proposals.title: The skeleton's shadow on the wall
proposals.versions: all five; matters most at Day, then Sunset and Dawn
proposals.observed: By Day the bone token (--isl-bone #efe8d6) is almost the wall's own colour (#e3ddd0 to #f1ece2). The ribs, arms and legs nearly vanish, and only the skull's eye holes and the dark stand read (day whole and 3x). The legs also fade into the lower wall at Sunset (#dcc3a4) and Dawn (#c3b8b8). The skeleton is one of the page's at-a-glance signs.
proposals.proposal: Draw a soft offset shadow of the skeleton on the wall behind it: the bones path in the wall-shadow tone at about 0.22 opacity, and the skull and pelvis in isl-tdrop, shifted by the same offset the calendar, whiteboard and flip chart use. The bones then separate from the wall in every version.
proposals.why: A cast shadow is the site's own way of setting a thing in front of its wall (the tdrop drops). It keeps the drawing and fixes the Day legibility without a new colour. The alternative, a deeper Day --isl-bone, only fixes one version.
proposals.code: lectureHall(): factor the skull and pelvis fill path from line 2403-2404 into a const `bonesF`. Before line 2401 add `s += `<g transform="translate(${F(Y(0.01))} ${F(Y(0.013))})"><path class="isl-mbshadow" d="${bones}" stroke-width="${F(Math.max(1, u * 0.2))}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${bonesF}"/></g>`;`. layout-art.css near line 664: `.isl .isl-mbshadow { stroke: var(--isl-lside); stroke-opacity: 0.22; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }`.

proposals.title: Sills and head reveals for the high windows
proposals.observed: The three high windows are a frame and two mullions cut into the wall, with no sill and no depth. The other interiors' windows (windowWall) have a projecting sill and a shaded reveal.
proposals.proposal: Under each window add a thin projecting sill in the frame's colour, a little wider than the frame, with a faint isl-tdrop shadow under it. At the head add a narrow isl-lsidew strip: the soffit, which is seen from below, since the eye (horizon Y(0.27)) is near the windows' foot.
proposals.why: This gives the wall thickness and matches the finish of the other three interiors. It is a small structural return, like the Court House corner the owner liked.
proposals.code: lectureHall(), after line 2376: `let sills = '', sh = '', heads = ''; for (const x of wins) { sills += rect(x - Y(0.015), wB, ww + Y(0.03), Math.max(2, Y(0.018))); sh += rect(x - Y(0.015), wB + Math.max(2, Y(0.018)), ww + Y(0.03), Math.max(1.2, Y(0.01))); heads += rect(x, wT, ww, Math.max(1.5, Y(0.015))); } s += `<path class="isl-lsidew" d="${heads}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${sh}"/><path class="isl-lsill" d="${sills}"/>`;`. Draw heads before the frame strokes so the frame stays crisp.

proposals.title: The water jug's handle is on its spout side
proposals.observed: The jug's top edge rises to a lip at jx + 0.09 m (the spout, on the right). Its handle (isl-kglassh) also starts at jx + 0.075 m and loops out to the right. Spout and handle are on the same side (3x right half, 305-368 x 352-425).
proposals.proposal: Mirror the handle to the left side, opposite the spout.
proposals.why: A pitcher's handle is always opposite its spout. This is the jug's version of 'a door on the wrong face': a small contradiction that reads as wrong once seen.

proposals.title: The lampshade's underside is missing by Day
proposals.versions: Day (the other four already show it lit)
proposals.observed: The shade's opening, the ellipse ring(0, D, 0.27, 1.7) that the eye 1.2 m up must see from below, is drawn only as the lit isl-tbulb inside the isl-vlamps group. By Day that group is display:none (layout-art.css line 155). So the shade becomes a flat-bottomed trapezoid, as if seen at eye level, while the table and chairs below are seen from above (3x day right half, 119-292 x 130-135).
proposals.proposal: Always draw the opening in an unlit tone (the shade's colour darkened by isl-tdrop) under the lit one. By Day the shade then shows its dark inside. From Dawn to Night the glowing underside covers it as now.
proposals.why: The one-camera rule the owner set for this room: everything obeys the same eye. At 1920 the opening is about 10 by 56 CSS px, so its absence by Day reads as a lamp from a different viewpoint.
proposals.code: committeeRoom(), after the lbronze rim on line 2672 and before the tbulb group on 2673: `+ `<path class="isl-cshade" d="${polyD(under)}"/><path class="isl-tdrop" d="${polyD(under)}"/>``.

proposals.title: A marker tray under the project board
proposals.observed: The whiteboard is a framed rectangle with a drop shadow, three columns and notes. Its lower edge is plain.
proposals.proposal: Along the board's lower edge add the pen ledge: a thin tray in the frame's aluminium, about 80% of the board's width and 3.5 cm deep in the camera, with its own small shadow. One dark marker lies on it.
proposals.why: This is the whiteboard's version of a sill. It is the detail that makes a white panel read as a working board, and fits 'Committee Work' (work in progress) at a glance. At 1920 the tray is about 2 by 104 CSS px and the marker about 8 by 1.5 px, so it reads at 2x.
proposals.code: committeeRoom(), inside `if (bw > Y(0.24))` after line 2523: `const ty0 = bT + bh, th = Math.max(2, 0.035 * sc(dW)), mh = Math.max(1.5, 0.02 * sc(dW)); s += `<path class="isl-tdrop" d="${rect(bx0 + bw * 0.08 + Y(0.006), ty0 + Y(0.008), bw * 0.84, th)}"/><path class="isl-lalu" d="${rect(bx0 + bw * 0.08, ty0, bw * 0.84, th)}"/><path class="isl-tiron" d="${rect(bx0 + bw * 0.62, ty0 - mh, 0.13 * sc(dW), mh)}"/>`;`.

proposals.title: A shadow under the window sill
proposals.versions: all five. windowWall is shared, so it also applies to hospital-room and week-calendar
proposals.observed: The sill projects past the frame by H*0.02 each side. It sits flat on the wall, with no shadow below it.
proposals.proposal: Under the sill's front edge add a thin soft isl-tdrop band, the full width of the sill, about H*0.012 deep.
proposals.why: The corner-turning kind of addition the owner praised: 'a shadow cast under an eave' makes the sill project, and gives the window wall a thickness it only half has now.
proposals.code: windowWall(), line 2202: append `+ `<path class="isl-tdrop" d="${rect(wx0 - H * 0.02, wB + Math.max(2, H * 0.022), ww + H * 0.04, Math.max(1.5, H * 0.012))}"/>``. In hospital-room the chair's back ends at wx0 - 0.04H, left of the sill, so they do not meet.

proposals.title: The boats' reflections in the window view
proposals.versions: all five. windowView is shared, so it also applies to hospital-room (one boat) and week-calendar
proposals.observed: The far land is mirrored in the window's water (mirrored(y0, farLand, 0.16)). The boats, hull and mast, have no reflection. Only their masthead columns (by night) touch the water.
proposals.proposal: Mirror each boat about its own waterline at about 0.18 opacity: the hull flipped under itself, and the mast as a faint line running down into the water, cut off by the sill as the wall covers it.
proposals.why: DESIGN 19.3: reflections of 'every hull and sail', 'a mirror about each boat's own waterline'. The land's reflection makes the missing boat reflections stand out.
proposals.code: windowView(), in the boats loop at lines 2213-2219: `const hd = `M${F(bx - hw)} ${F(by - Y(0.015) * k)}H${F(bx + hw)}L${F(bx + hw * 0.72)} ${F(by)}H${F(bx - hw * 0.78)}Z`, md = `M${F(bx)} ${F(by - Y(0.015) * k)}V${F(by - mh)}`; s += `<g transform="translate(0 ${F(2 * by)}) scale(1 -1)" opacity=".18"><path class="isl-vhull" d="${hd}"/><path class="isl-vmast" d="${md}" stroke-width=".8"/></g>`;`. Then `hulls += hd; masts += md;` as now, so the boats draw over their reflections.

checked_fine: hospital-room: window frame, mullion, transom and sill are aligned. The reveal shade is on the right jamb. The blinds' slats stop just above the transom, and the pull cords hang past them into the lower panes as real cords do.

hospital-room: at Sunset the Sun (18:23) stands on the far hill in the right pane with its path on the water. Dawn has no Sun (the window faces the setting bearing). Day has no lights. Night has no horizon glow. Dusk keeps a thin warm glow in the view.
hospital-room: the bright point among the upper slats at Dusk and Night is a planet at the Moon's baked offset, not a misplaced Moon. A Moon disc at moonBig 1.1 would be about 22 CSS px across.
hospital-room: the heartbeat trace in the page's hue is the only kind accent. The monitor is always on. The lamp is lit Dawn to Night with its halo and cone, and off by Day.

hospital-room: the bed's head is raised with a pillow, a blanket and a side rail, with head and foot posts and a wheel at each end. The chair faces the bed. The curtain hangs from its track with the hem clear of the floor and the folds following the gather.
hospital-room: at 1440 the composition holds, with the chair about 10 CSS px clear of the bed's foot (see hospital-room-7 for narrower widths).

lecture-hall: the heart on the screen is in the kind hue with its vessels and septum, and the notes are beside it. The screen is lit in every version. The lectern lamp's halo is on from Dawn to Night and off by Day.

lecture-hall: seen from the audience, the laptop shows the back of its lid, which is correct. The skeleton hangs with its feet above the base, as on a real stand, and the base is hidden by the front rail. The ribs taper and the pelvis sits where the legs start.
lecture-hall: the high windows show the right sky per version (Dawn purple, Sunset red, Dusk near-dark, Night stars) over a line of far hills. There is no Sun (sunPath false) and no grain on land.
lecture-hall: the nearer seat row is larger, lower and darker than the far row, as depth demands.

committee-room: one true perspective throughout. The floorboards meet on the window's horizon, the chairs are sized and shadowed at their own depths, and the far chairs' seats are hidden by the table (accepted).
committee-room: the flip chart's right front leg splays far more than the left. At about 4.2 m off the camera axis at 4.5 m depth, this is what the single camera gives, not a drawing error.
committee-room: the window's reveal is on the left jamb, the one a camera to its right would see. The sill projects past the frame.

committee-room: the lamp set is complete from Dawn to Night: halo, cone, pool on the table and the table's near edge catching the light. The flip chart's three ticks are in the kind hue (the only accent), with the last tick last in the pass.

committee-room: the board is framed with a drop shadow and three columns, the done column fullest. Each place has its papers, name card and glass, and the minutes are stacked in folders with their tabs. The open folder with its pen sits at the viewer's own place.
committee-room: at Sunset the Sun stands on the far hill in the right pane with its path. The bright dot in the top-left pane at night is a planet at the Moon's offset, not the Moon.

All three pieces at 1920 and 1440 in every version: no truncated or broken shapes were seen that would suggest a NaN or a stray H/V run-on. The attributes were not scanned, since this pass was read-only.
All three: no starless boxes, no grain on the interiors' solid forms, and every light is hidden by Day. Nothing overlaps page text: the pictures are self-contained heads.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in every version. In the day whole image the wheel bottoms sit at about y=389 and the floor line at 407 (2x), so the bed hangs about 9 CSS px above the floor. The chair's legs end exactly on the line, which makes the bed's float stand out even more. The code agrees: bLeg is Y(0.8), the wheels are centred at Y(0.83) with r Y(0.03), and fl is Y(0.9). The drip stand's base is at fl - Y(0.02). Every variable the change needs is in scope. With bLeg at Y(0.87) the legs meet the wheel tops and the wheels straddle the skirting, so they read as standing on the floor in front of the wall. The long thin tdrop under the bed is a plausible floor shadow. This is exactly the 'floating' flaw the owner catches.

Confirmed. In the day 3x left half the hook bar is at y about 88 and the bag top at about 100, a visible gap of about 4 CSS px with nothing between them. The bar's right end, ix+Y(0.05), is the bag's centre, so the hanger is one short vertical stroke. The bag's lowest point is at about bagB-Y(0.005), so the chamber rect starting at bagB-Y(0.006) joins it cleanly, and starting the line at bagB+Y(0.03) meets the chamber's foot. The drip chamber is a true, recognisable detail that suits Clinical Practice, at about 3 by 8 CSS px.

Confirmed. The arm is a round-capped lalu stub (x 516 to 556, y 162 in the day 3x half) that ends on the bare wall. A 4 by 16 px plate over its left cap reads as a wall mount and clears the headboard, the bag and the IV line. The optional monitor drop shadow does little, since tiron on the dark Dusk and Night walls barely separates either way. Take the plate, and treat the shadow as optional.

Confirmed in the hospital night 3x right half and the committee night 3x left half. The six hill lights have no column, and only the mastheads have their dashes. The windowView comment and DESIGN 19.4 both promise the set. The code is feasible: dashes, streakList and rng are module level. A separate rng(4057) keeps the boats' streaks and the week-calendar shrubs unchanged. The wall covers everything below wB, and s-vglow is already hidden by Day. The streaks' visible part lies in streakList's top bucket, so they show at 0.18, fainter than the boats' 0.3. It is small in a small window, but it is the stated method.

The cone ends on the blanket, so it does not quite stop 'in the air'. Its foot at bTop-Y(0.04) is about 2 px below the blanket's top edge at lx, where the edge is at about bTop-Y(0.051). Still, a pool completes the lamp's set, as the committee table's pool does. I checked the ellipse: its top reaches the blanket edge only at its centre, where the gradient is already near zero, so it stays on the blanket. It is inside the isl-vlamps group, so it is off by Day. Marginal but harmless. Pair it with the lamp's missing lit underside (see the missed item), which is the bigger gap in this set.

True to hospitals (cubicle curtains do have a mesh top), and the owner, a medical educator, would recognise it. But the code as written fills the band with url(#islhwallg). That gradient is in objectBoundingBox units, so it restretches the whole wall gradient over the 19 px band: a blended tint, not the wall seen through. The fold paths would also run through the band. A 0.6 px grid at 0.16 opacity will not read on its own, so what reads is the pale band and its seam.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Split the curtain instead of overlaying it. Start the fabric path, and each fold line, at mB = Y(0.13) instead of Y(0.045). Above it, draw the band rect(-2, Y(0.045), cx1 + 2 + Y(0.004), mB - Y(0.045)) as class isl-hcurtain with fill-opacity .35, so the real wall shows through. Over it lay the grid (isl-hfold, stroke-width .6) and a seam line (isl-hfold, max(1, Y(0.01))) at mB. No new gradient is needed. Check at 1920 that the band reads as a paler open band, not as a separate valance.

verdicts.reason: Not visible in any render. At 1920 the gap from the chair seat to the footboard is about 14 CSS px, and at 1440 about 9 px, both clear. The two renders have W/H of 3.59 and 3.30, and H shrank from 227 to 206 as the window narrowed. Extrapolating gives W/H of about 3.0 at 1120, still a positive gap of a few px, well away from the 2.67 needed for contact. The clamp would also push the chair's back in front of the window and sill if it ever engaged. The 1280/1120 look in the normal review loop (DESIGN 19.5) is the right place to catch this if it happens.

Clearly visible. In the 1920 night and day whole images the third window runs under the screen frame (window 843 to 1005, frame from 1003) and loses its right frame. At 1440 about half its third pane is hidden. A collision and a broken rhythm are exactly what the owner catches. I checked the arithmetic. At 1920 the windows land at 97.7, 252.4 and 407.1 CSS px with 73 px gaps, and the third ends about 13 px short of the frame. At 1440 the gaps are 51.5 px and the margin 12 px. The moonAt change to (W*0.37 - H*0.035)/W is the new middle window's centre. The skeleton stays in front of the third window's left part, as it is now.

Confirmed. In the day whole image, white vertical slivers run from the second rail to the bottom edge at x about 245, 720 and 1195, and the pale wall shows between every seat. At dusk and night the lower wall's lighter gradient shows the same way. The lectern's foot (to Y(0.84)) and the skeleton's pole and base also show below the front rail between the seats. The band from Y(0.78) is drawn before the rows, so each rail covers the band's top edge, and the band hides the lectern and stand below the rail. Both then stand behind the rail, which DESIGN 19.3 calls occlusion that grounds a thing. The floor tone keeps the seat shapes readable, and a band in the seat colour would merge the second row into it.

Confirmed in the night 3x right half: the arms hang as separate sticks beside the rib cage, with no shoulder girdle. The top rib ends at about ±0.86u, and the arms start at ±1.1u, 0.45u higher. The clavicle curve meets the humerus start exactly and crosses under the jaw at top+1.55u. At about 11 px u it reads as the shoulder line, and on the Medical Education page an unattached arm is the kind of anatomical slip the owner's audience notices. The hands and feet are optional and marginal: 5 px and 3 px strokes read as slightly longer limbs rather than as hands.

Confirmed. A pale, lopsided wedge shows at the top edge above the screen (about 1050 to 1340, y 0 to 30 in the 2x night and sunset images), with no source. The beam polygon also skips (sx1, sT), which is why the part above the screen is lopsided. With the lens at Y(0.035), the part above the frame becomes a thin fan about 7 px tall, so the stray patch mostly goes, and a small hung projector explains the light. A 25 by 6 px box hanging above the screen's middle is the right scale for a ceiling projector. The code is feasible: polyD and rect are in scope, and the body ends at Y(0.04), clear of the frame at Y(0.068). It is modest, and it keeps and fixes the feature rather than removing it.

Confirmed and important for the at-a-glance test. By Day the skeleton almost vanishes: --isl-bone #efe8d6 sits on a #e3ddd0 to #f1ece2 wall, and only the eye holes and the stand read. At Sunset and Dawn the legs fade into the lighter lower wall. A darker Day token would not fix Sunset and Dawn, where the wall runs from darker at the top to lighter at the bottom behind the figure. A cast shadow fixes all five, and the committee room's flip chart already sets the precedent of a tdrop on a free-standing object. But at the proposed offset of Y(0.01), Y(0.013) (about 2.3 by 3 px) each rib's shadow lands in the middle of the roughly 4 px gap below it. The rib cage then turns into a striped, doubled skeleton rather than a separated one.
verdicts.revised_proposal: Add the same shadow group (bones in a new isl-mbshadow stroke of --isl-lside at about 0.22, and the skull and pelvis factored into bonesF in isl-tdrop), drawn before the bones. Offset it by about half as much, translate(Y(0.005), Y(0.007)), so each bone gains a thin shaded edge on its lower-right side instead of a ghost copy. Leave the stand without a shadow. Check the rib cage at 1920 Day and at 1440 Sunset.

verdicts.reason: Observation correct: the high windows are bare frames cut into the wall, while windowWall gives the other interiors a sill and a shaded reveal. The geometry is right. The eye at Y(0.27) is just above the windows' foot at Y(0.3), so the head's soffit is seen from below and the sill's top barely shows. The sill and head strip are small (3 to 4 px) but give the wall thickness, like the Court House return. The code note contradicts itself: it says to insert after line 2376, the frame strokes, but also to draw the heads before the frame.
verdicts.revised_proposal: As proposed, but insert the isl-lsidew head strips before line 2376, so the frame and mullion strokes stay crisp over them. Add the tdrop shadow and the isl-lsill sill after line 2376. Build it on the re-spaced windows of lecture-hall-1.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the day and night 3x right halves: the jug's lip rises to a spout at the top right (jx+0.09 m), and the handle loops out on the same right side. The mirrored handle reaches about jx-0.155 m. That clears the far place's glass, about 25 px away at 3x, and the folders at x -0.34 m. It is a small contradiction of the 'door on the wrong face' kind, and the fix is a one-line sign flip.

Confirmed. By Day the shade ends in a flat bronze rim, a trapezoid seen at eye level, while from Dawn to Night the owner-approved glowing underside shows the opening from below, as the one camera requires (eye 1.2 m, rim 1.7 m). The polyD(under) ring is in scope. The unlit copy sits under the tbulb, which covers it exactly in the lit versions. By Day the lower half of the ellipse hangs below the rim against the pale wall, so the shade reads as a round shade seen from below, consistent with the table and chairs.

A true, low-risk addition: bT, bh, bx0, bw and sc are in scope inside the board block. At 1920, sc(dW) is about 59 px/m, so the tray is about 2 by 110 px, just under the aluminium frame's 1.7 px bottom edge. It reads as a ledge rather than clearly as a pen tray, and the 8 by 1.5 px marker only reads as a dark dash. The notes and columns already carry 'work in progress'. Marginal gain, no clutter.

Confirmed: the sill is a flat lframe band with no shadow under it in all three interiors that share windowWall. The shadow band is a one-line addition with the variables in scope. In the hospital room the chair's back ends about 4.5 px left of the sill, and in the committee room the left chair, drawn later, simply covers the shadow's end. A small projecting-edge finish of the kind the owner liked.

Confirmed: the land is mirrored in the window water but the hulls and masts are not, in all five versions (day and dusk renders). The DESIGN 19.3 table asks for 'every hull and sail'. The code is feasible. Mirroring about each boat's own waterline puts the reflection only in the water, and the wall, drawn after, crops the mast's reflection at the sill. Drawing it before the hulls keeps the boats over their reflections. The hulls are about 3 px tall, so the gain is small, but it matches the land's reflection beside them.

proposals.title: Turn the corner: shade the coping and string course over the side face
proposals.observed: The building's left end shows a narrow side face in shade (isl-vpshade strip, b0 to b0+0.035H), with the quoins on the front face beside it. The shade stops under the coping. The coping, which projects 0.012H past b0, runs across the top of the side face in full light. The string course between the floors (at mid, 0.4H) also crosses the shaded strip in lit stone. This shows in every version, most clearly in the Day and Dusk 3x left halves.
proposals.proposal: Carry the side face's shade up through both courses. Shade the coping's share of the side face, offset by its projection: b0-0.012H to b0+0.023H, from bTop-0.03H to bTop. Shade the string course's share too: b0 to b0+0.035H, across its 0.018H height. The side face then reads as one plane from the pavement to the coping.
proposals.why: This is the same fault as the Old Court House before today's fix. A drawing that shows two faces must keep to them all the way up; otherwise the top of the building does not turn the corner. The owner called that fixed corner 'an absolutely beautiful addition'. Note: the Court House's own string course (courtHouse line 1191) still crosses its shaded side face in lit stone. It can be seen as the light band between the floors in court-house_1920_day_right-half_3x.png, so the same one-rect turn would finish that corner too.
proposals.code: wayIn, after line 2727 (the under-coping vpshade): s += `<path class="isl-vpshade" d="${rect(b0 - Y(0.012), bTop - Y(0.03), Y(0.035), Y(0.03))}${rect(b0, mid - Y(0.008), Y(0.035), Y(0.018))}"/>`; This mirrors courtHouse's turn(a, b, o) at lines 1183-1184, where each course's share of the side face is offset by its own projection (0.012H for the coping; the string course is flush at b0). The s-rim on the coping's top edge (line 2728) stays as it is.

proposals.title: Stone lintels over the windows, to pair with the sills
proposals.observed: Every window has a projecting stone sill (isl-vstone). Above the openings there is only a vpshade 'head' band inside the top of the glass, so the tops of the openings are cut straight into the coursed stone with nothing to carry the wall over them. At night the head reads as a dark band across the top of each lit pane.
proposals.proposal: Add a flat stone lintel above each opening, slightly wider than the window (ww + 0.016H) and 0.02H tall, in the same isl-vstone as the sills. Upper floor: from bTop+0.03H to bTop+0.05H, between the coping's shadow band and the window head. Ground floor: from dT-0.02H to dT, sitting on the rusticated course at 0.50H. The existing heads then read as the lintel's shadow in the window reveal.
proposals.why: The building is rusticated stone with quoins, a string course and a coping. Openings in walls like this have a lintel over each one, and a sill without its lintel leaves the window half-framed. At 1920 the lintels would be about 38 by 5 CSS px, and at mid-height they are lighter than the facade gradient there, so they read.

proposals.title: A halo round the station's lit windows, and a rim on its roof edge

proposals.title: A concrete plinth and contact shadow under the dish's pedestal
proposals.observed: The two lattice legs end as bare line ends on the grass (footY 0.68H, just below the crest at 0.661H). Nothing shows the largest object in the picture being anchored to the ground.
proposals.proposal: Draw a low concrete plinth under the pedestal: 0.22H wide by 0.026H tall, centred on the feet, drawn after the truss so the leg ends are set into it. Draw it in isl-aramp, the file's poured-concrete token, over a soft contact shadow (an isl-tdrop ellipse slightly wider than the plinth).
proposals.why: A radio dish stands on a concrete foundation. The finish's grounding rule is occlusion or a contact shadow that stops a thing from floating. At 1920 the plinth would be about 50 by 6 CSS px, readable at the picture's size.
proposals.code: dishNet, after the truss path (line 2437): s += `<ellipse class="isl-tdrop" cx="${F(dx)}" cy="${F(footY + Y(0.012))}" rx="${F(Y(0.15))}" ry="${F(Y(0.02))}"/><path class="isl-aramp" d="${rect(dx - Y(0.11), footY - Y(0.012), Y(0.22), Y(0.026))}"/>`; The bowl's lowest point (rimB, about 0.59H) stays well above it.

proposals.title: The yoke: fork arms up to an elevation bearing on the dish's side
proposals.observed: The comment at line 2434 promises 'a lattice pedestal, the yoke, the bowl', but no yoke is drawn. The lattice legs run up behind the bowl and vanish into its lower edge (about 0.51H at dx), so the dish seems to rest on the tower rather than turn on it.
proposals.proposal: Continue each leg's own line from just below the bowl's edge (footY-0.15H, where each leg is at dx±0.05H) up over the bowl's side, converging on a small dark bearing hub at (dx, pivY+0.1H). This hub lies inside the bowl, about 0.07H behind the rim. It is the near fork arm and the elevation axis the dish tilts on.
proposals.why: This detail is typical of the real thing: a steerable dish is held in a fork by its elevation bearing, and that is what lets it be 'turned to the sky'. Because the arms continue the visible legs from below the bowl's edge, there is no gap where a leg disappears and reappears.

proposals.title: Give the bowl its roundness: a shaded band along its back
proposals.versions: all five (isl-lsidew is 0.18 opacity, 0.1 by Day)
proposals.observed: The bowl, the biggest form in the picture, is one flat fill: white by Day, light grey at Dusk, mid grey at Night. Nothing tells the eye it is a curved shell.
proposals.proposal: Between the bowl fill and its rim line, lay a crescent of isl-lsidew along the convex back. Its outer edge is the bowl's own back curve and its inner edge a shallower curve (control at pivot - 1.2·u·depth), so the band is widest at the back's apex (0.4 × depth, about 15 CSS px at 1920) and tapers to nothing at both rim tips.
proposals.why: The back faces down and right, away from the sunset glow at the left and from the high Day sun, so darkening where it turns away most follows the real face of the form. Because it follows the bowl's own curves, it avoids the 'stray patch' the owner warned about, and it gives the dish volume at every width.
proposals.code: dishNet, between the isl-ddish and isl-ddish2 paths (lines 2440-2441): `<path class="isl-lsidew" d="M${F(rimA[0])} ${F(rimA[1])}Q${F(dx - 2 * ux * depth)} ${F(pivY - 2 * uy * depth)} ${F(rimB[0])} ${F(rimB[1])}Q${F(dx - 1.2 * ux * depth)} ${F(pivY - 1.2 * uy * depth)} ${F(rimA[0])} ${F(rimA[1])}Z"/>`. It is one closed subpath, so there is no winding trap. The outer control equals the existing back[0] - ux*depth.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the Day, Dusk and Night 3x left halves. The coping runs lit across the top of the olive side strip, and the string course crosses it as a light band at about y=292 (3x). In the code, the coping rect starts at b0-Y(0.012) (line 2726), the string course rect starts at b0, and both are drawn after the side-strip vpshade (line 2718). The offsets match courtHouse's turn(a,b,o), mirrored for a left-hand face: the projecting coping turns at b0+0.023H, and the flush string course turns at b0+0.035H. This is the same fault as today's Court House fix, and the owner called that fixed corner beautiful. It is two rects in the existing vpshade class and adds no clutter.

On the upper floor, the coping's shadow band covers bTop to bTop+0.02H (line 2727) and the windows start at bTop+0.05H. A lintel at bTop+0.03 to 0.05H leaves a strip of wall only about 2.3 CSS px tall between two bands. That makes a striped stack under the coping, not a clear frame. On the ground floor, a lintel at 0.50 to 0.52H lands on the rusticated joint at 0.50H (mid+0.05H, line 2720). Plain openings over projecting sills are a normal treatment for stone buildings like this, so the window is not really 'half-framed'. The existing head band reads correctly as the reveal's shadow in the Night 3x render.

Confirmed. The planter is isl-vstone (line 2816). The facade gradient (islvfacade, objectBoundingBox from bTop to street) is already about 92 to 100% vstone over the planter's height, so the box has no edge in any version. In the Day and Dusk right halves and at 1440, the shrubs look as if they sit on a ledge of the wall. isl-aramp differs from the wall in every version: #c3c8cd against #cdbfa3 by Day, #7e8690 against #a39a86 at Dusk, #2c323b against #3b4049 at Night. It also matches the ramp and steps it stands beside. The vstep-edge lip and the foot shadow reuse the stair's own treatment, and every class is defined in all five versions.

The Court House corner the owner praised has quoins on its front face only (line 1197, at x1-qw). Its side face is plain shade, so this proposal departs from the approved model. Blocks the full width of the 8.5 CSS px strip would replace the vstrata-toned facade under the shade with lighter vstone. That weakens the shade the corner depends on, and the 1.2 px joints every 11 px would read as a ladder. It is a detail that does not read when stylised.

The inconsistency is real in theory: fanning from 0.5W puts the eye right of a corner whose left face is visible. But the fan is a loose texture gesture. Its convergence point sits about 1.75H above the street, nowhere near the horizon, and the ramp, landing and steps are drawn in pure elevation, which agrees with no vanishing point at all. Nobody sees the current fan as wrong at stroke-opacity .5 and width .7. The change makes the right-hand joints lean harder (0.049W against 0.04W now), under the building and the door, where the eye is. The proposal also contradicts itself: the text says 0.06, the code says 0.07. It is a risk with no visible gain.

Real, as the geometry and the Day render show. The floor is at 0.72H. The crest is at 0.76H at the left wall (0.64W) and reaches the floor only at its vertex (0.67W). The shrub at [0.64, 0.77] reaches about 0.652W, but its right-hand crowns top out near 0.738H, below the floor. That leaves a pale sliver of sky about 4 CSS px tall and 11 px wide under the floor by Day. The draw-before-the-land approach is sound, and hoisting bx, bT and bw is needed to avoid a use-before-declaration (TDZ) error.
verdicts.revised_proposal: As proposed, but fill the footing with isl-aramp rather than isl-tw0: s += `<path class="isl-aramp" d="${rect(bx, bT + Y(0.14) - 1, bw, Y(0.08))}"/>` before the land path (after hoisting bx, bT and bw above line 2427). The downhill end then reads as a concrete footing meeting the slope, and it continues the base course proposed as dish-net-7, so the station sits on one poured base. If dish-net-7 is not taken, isl-tw0 (the wall carried down) is the better fill.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night: three hard-edged lit rectangles on a block with no glow. DESIGN 19.3 and 19.4 ask for a halo on every window cluster. The code, however, uses the default islvbulb (centre opacity .5). The near stone house in Betty's Hope, the closest analogue, uses the softer islvwarm (.26) at Y(0.25) for a window cluster on a wall (line 1043). A .5 bulb spread over a dark near wall would blot the facade. The roof rim is right: the roof faces the afterglow side, s-rim is hidden at Night on its own, and DESIGN lists roofs for rims.
verdicts.revised_proposal: After the isl-troof path: `<g class="isl-vwin" style="--i:0">${halo(bx + Y(0.15), bT + Y(0.065), Y(0.2), 'islvwarm')}</g>` (centred on the window cluster, not the whole block), plus the rim as proposed: `<path class="s-rim" d="M${F(bx - Y(0.01))} ${F(bT - Y(0.015) + 0.5)}H${F(bx + bw + Y(0.01))}" stroke-width="1" stroke-opacity=".4"/>`.

verdicts.reason: The blank right bay is real. The openings end at bx+0.26H of a 0.36H front, with a 0.04H margin on the left and 0.10H on the right. The proposed door evens the rhythm (gaps 0.04, 0.04, 0.035; margins 0.04 and 0.03), keeps off the corner, and reaches the floor where the station is drawn over the rising hill (the crest there is about 0.687H, above the 0.72H floor). The pool at 0.735H lands on the land in front. It is a small, coherent light set but a modest gain. If dish-net-7's base course is taken, stop the door at bT+Y(0.126) so it stands on the course.

The legs do end as bare line ends at footY, and a pad under a dish's pedestal is realistic and grounds the biggest object in the picture. The proposed size collides at 1440, though. There W/H is about 3.3, the shrub at [0.9, 0.7] starts only about 0.12H right of dx, and its crowns about 0.13H right. A plinth to dx+0.11H touches it, and a shadow of rx 0.15H spreads over the shrub's lower left, since the shrubs are drawn earlier in section 1.
verdicts.revised_proposal: After the truss path: `<ellipse class="isl-tdrop" cx="${F(dx)}" cy="${F(footY + Y(0.01))}" rx="${F(Y(0.115))}" ry="${F(Y(0.016))}"/><path class="isl-aramp" d="${rect(dx - Y(0.1), footY - Y(0.012), Y(0.2), Y(0.024))}"/>`. Each foot then sits 0.02H inside the pad's ends and clears the shrub at both 1920 and 1440. Check the 1440 render before showing the owner.

verdicts.reason: A yoke is true to real dishes, but this version would not read. The arms are isl-dtruss (--isl-lalu) laid over the bowl (--isl-lframe): #b7bcc2 on #a3a7ae at Dusk, #6c7178 on #5a5e66 at Night, and #d5d9de on #fafafa by Day. They would all but vanish, leaving a dark isl-tiron dot on the dish that reads as a blemish. The right leg also meets the bowl's edge at about 0.49H, not 0.53H, so the right arm would split off the visible leg below the rim in a small forked 'Y'. It is a detail that does not read when stylised.

Confirmed: the bowl is one flat fill in all five versions. The crescent follows the bowl's own back curve (its outer control equals back - u*depth) and tapers to the rim tips. It darkens the lower-right limb, which faces away from both the sunset side and a high sun, so it follows a real face of the form rather than making a stray patch. Its width is about 0.4 × depth ≈ 14 CSS px at 1920. isl-lsidew is 0.1 by Day and 0.18 otherwise (layout-art.css lines 492-493), so it stays quiet. It is one closed subpath with no winding trap. The gain in volume is modest but real.

missed.observed: Five lights stand on the far headland's slopes at Dawn, Sunset, Dusk and Night (lines 2699-2702; seen as dots at about y=430 in the Night 3x left half). By Day, s-vlight is hidden (layout-art.css line 155) and nothing takes their place, so the headland is bare in the Day render. The other pieces with far lights on land draw a Day-only house at each light with makeKit(W, H).dayHouses: lines 688, 762, 920, 1018 and 1309. That follows the owner's 2026-09-28 rule that a building by Day is the one whose windows are lit at night (comment at line 316, and DESIGN 19.6).
missed.proposal: After the far lights, draw Day-only houses at those points. Keep only the points where a house's roof stays under the headland's crest. Size them like the cathedral's far houses. They are white walls with red or grey roofs a few CSS px across, as on the other pieces' far shores.
missed.why: It is the piece's one departure from a convention the owner set and every comparable piece follows. The Day version then shows the same village whose windows light at dusk.
missed.code: wayIn, after line 2702: s += makeKit(W, H).dayHouses(far.filter(([x, y]) => crestAt(x) - (y0 - y) > Y(0.017)), Y(0.012), 97); dayHouses uses its own rng seed, so r() and the rest of the piece are undisturbed. It returns an isl-ydet group, so it shows by Day only. crestAt (line 2696) returns the headland's height above y0 at x.
